This is probably not going to be that big of a deal to many players, but I basically can't play video games that don't have programmable keys. I broke my arm when I was a kid and I have a plate with 11 screws holding together my humerus bone. To put the plate in they had to cut through and destroy most the muscles. Doesn't effect MOST of my day to day life much, I've learned to manage, but with gaming I can't use a mouse in my right hand. I can't move my wrist/hand with enough precision or quickly enough but flicking my fingers around is still fine, so I learned to left hand mouse and use the arrow keys/number pad.

Even ignoring that, I know I also like to program the same command to the same buttons. I think the current rating system is flawed. You only get 50 points to spend on rating per day, so most people will want to spend them as fast as possible to get their brick points by just spending 10 points at a time, skewing the ratings upwards. And if they don't rate everything a 10, then when they get down to having less than 10 points left, they can only rate a map for as many points as they have. For example, if someone rates 4 maps a 10, and one map a 9, if they want spend all of their star dust, they'll have to rate a map a 1. This is unfair to that maps developer. A suggested fix should be that you have to rate 5ish maps per day to get all of your brick points, and any ratings after that don't give you brick points, but still affect the map's rating.

Also, I think you should only be allowed to rate a map once. Unless you want to change your rating, of course.

As I have not messed with the rating system, I don't really know how it works, but after reading what you said I think you are right, it is unfair the map makers for no reason. You should be able to vote for any maps 1 time and I don't think there should be a daily limit, right now that does really matter since there isn't alot of maps, but when there is a tons of players making new maps its going to be hard to give them credit where credit is due. I understand why you get brick points (to encourage people to rate more I suppose) but that also seems a little silly as most will just do what you said and spam there points out right away to any map. You should get points for writing small reviews about the maps or maybe for a more in depth rating systems on top of 1 - 10 style rating system. When I say more in depth I mean there are 5 categories to give maps points in, such as Spawn points, Balancing, creativity, etc.

Originally Posted by gnarvin
As I have not messed with the rating system, I don't really know how it works...
Ah, yes. I should've explained how it works. Well, basically you get 50 "Star Dust" per day. You use these Star Dust to rate maps. You must use 1 Star Dust per point in your rating. So if you rate a map a 10, you must use 10 Star Dusts. When you have less than 10 Star Dust, the maximum rating you can give is the amount you have.

Also, I think the in-depth rating system like the one you proposed would give developers great feedback.

I think the Star Dust system would have worked fine if the displayed map rating is a cumulative score rather than a rolling average. That way, giving a 1 point rating because you only have one left to give will not affect the maps' scores negatively.

It should also be changed so that you could only rate a map once per day. So if you give a rating to, say...COD Battleship, you cannot give a rating to that map until the next day, you must spend your remaining stardust on another map.

I think the Star Dust system would have worked fine if the displayed map rating is a cumulative score rather than a rolling average. That way, giving a 1 point rating because you only have one left to give will not affect the maps' scores negatively.
While it would be slightly better, it would still be a little flawed, as the maps played earlier in the day will have a higher rating because more people will still have their Star Dust left.
Spamming something won't make that thing better so... I think this is normal and good.

Originally Posted by ImTheFool
While it would be slightly better, it would still be a little flawed, as the maps played earlier in the day will have a higher rating because more people will still have their Star Dust left.
But if you set a delay timer that prevents you from rating a map several times a day, and limit your rating of a specific map to something like once a day, or once every 2 days, it would balance out. Have it say "You have already rated this map today/in the last x days"

I think the problem is, as some people said, that a lot of people want to spend as much Star Dust as possible to get their brick points, thus making them rate 5 random maps, regardless of quality, a rating of 10.

This means that whatever map gets played the most in the beginning will be rated high, and since it's rated high it'll be played more, and there's going to be a vicious cycle.

It would be better if everyone got 10 Star Dust per day, and each time you rate a map it uses up 1 Star Dust, regardless of what you rate it. Of course, the amount of points you get per Star Dust spent has to go up.

title: Paying for Bricks and/or Maps is Flawed

posts.h:
This is another post of mine that explains one of the topics of my General fix/suggestion thread. Paying for Bricks and/or Maps is definitely broken. I know that it IS something that is probably a hot issue, as giving up your ability to sell bricks or the ability to put maps up would be frustrating; HOWEVER, making either of these things cost money hurts the game as a whole.

For example, let's say a user is REALLY GOOD at creating maps, but doesn't have the $$$ or in-game cash to buy the brick items. He will only be able to make a mediocre (at best) map only using the default bricks. While that user could've made the best map on the server had the bricks been available to him, he was only able to make a feeble attempt. This hurts everyone on the server because no one gets to play the epic map that could've been made. This would also hurt if someone had to put in less cover or decorations on a map they made because putting in more things would cost them more money that they don't have.

Another reason it hurts the game is because the main thing that draws people in is the ability to make their own maps. Sure, the gunplay is great (better than I expected it to be), but not everyone will be drawn in by that. And if people find out they can't actually make the maps they want to make because they can't use certain bricks or any decorations, they might never play BrickForce D:.

I think that the current system needs to be reworked some way. The least that could be done is to remove the buying of certain bricks. That way, everyone would always be able to build however they like. The map fee is still annoying because it delays great maps from being played by everyone. If a fee was necessary to continue your business model, I'd suggest lowering the map creation fee greatly or just making any map cost a fixed amount to publish (Like 10k, no matter the size or amount of decoration.)

tl;dr: Maps costing money makes people put less cool stuff in their maps, which hurts everyone's experience, not just their's.

I think a better solution would be to have a mastery level for each weapon that takes a while to train on. For each level of mastery you gain with a gun, the price to rent said gun is reduced. (No refunds.) Once you reach level 6 mastery with a weapon, it is permanently yours.

Another solution that could also be implemented would be a pack of permanently unlocked guns that could only be bought with either real money from the site, or a couple of million points on the ingame store.

While I would love a permanent shop, it messes with their business model, which relies on players spending money to keep buying guns. The more often they have to spend money, the more money Infernum will make. The only way around this would be to introduce new content often. This would only half-work with guns, as the new guns like wouldn't provide that much of a stat difference. However, I could definitely see this possible with clothes, assuming Infernum is willing to constantly introduce new clothes into the game. It would work with clothes because you can constantly introduce new clothes, and people will constantly buy them, assuming they are good enough. Everyone always wants a Santa Hat around Christmas time, or a Pumpkin Hat around Halloween, or scuba gear and flippers in the summer. And with those limited edition items, permanent purchases would be very likely. The permanent purchase could still apply to all clothes, too.

A lack of permanent options is leading to the death of games such as Repulse, games which had massive potential and were great fun. I don't know what everyone is so afraid of regarding permanent weapons, TF2 is perhaps the most successful f2p fps on the market and everything you buy from them you keep forever and ive never heard anyone complain about it, hell, their hat economy is valued at approximately $50,000,000. Personally in games like this I have an incentive to collect, to unlock better things, repaying virtually or not is quite frankly just boring, and im not about to pay for something that I do not get to keep. The trick to balancing the game out, between the newcomers, and those who have clogged say 200 hours and/or have bought a ton of stuff is to balance out what's on offer. Offer a weapon for example, which is both desirable, competes with stock weapons, yet is not op by comparison, so your free players will have a chance, but those who have unlocked more are having more fun by improving their inventory/character and are having more choice (or strategic choice)on the battlefield. This will give others an incentive to play more to unlock more, and, perhaps invest a little pocket money :P. Furthermore offer weapons etc that are reasonably priced according to their needs. for example, the super mega awesome orbital ion cannon that fires rainbow lazers? price it out of reach of most, or, make it take a lot of hard work to obtain. The trick to keeping an active user-base is to give them incentive to come back, and with a game like this, it will always be your unlocks, by not allowing me to keep what i have rightfully earned/paid for, i loose incentive and move onto better things that acquaint to my wants/needs, as will many others in the community.

This is an exceptionally interesting problem.

If you have temporary items then the assumption is people will keep spending money to buy items; people using normal points doesn't provide you guys with any income. I think the real question here is are people more psychologically motivated if they know they will 'own' something compared to if they can 'rent' something.

But then this broadens up because 'renting' has an inherent impermanence; for example if I rent a car it's usually because I'm abroad and if I rent a room it's because I don't intend to stay. If people are renting what they 'have' will be gone within a time period, a week at the moment. Now after that week they have nothing again and so have no vested interest, I think this may end in more people leaving because without an investment, you lose a lot of motivation. It's like that same response you get when you accidently lose a save game file and just think 'screw this'.

It goes much deeper than this, but I've just woke up, but honestly - really interesting conversation. But yeah I think the profit margin is the most important factor, but I think you'll make more money in the long run by attracting a wider audience and maintaining many who spend less than squeezing the few that spend more.

Aside from adding extra decorations and color blocks, (which I can't WAIT for!), it would be nice if Map editing was more advanced. Meaning, of course, there were more tools or roundabouts as to getting things done faster.

Swap Tool:
While building on a map I tend to make a guideline using a random block for such an activity. Usually, I don't have a specific color picked out for the whole map, so therefore I pick something random for the time. When things become finalized, I prepare my self for the time consuming block replacement method.

With the Swap Tool, I had the idea that you could highlight the amount of blocks in which you want to be replaced with a specified block to save time. Something along the lines of A - B Highlighting to change various amounts of blocks at once. and if its a Square or rectangle need to swapped, then A - B - C - D points and the rest of the square would fill in, (hoping you catch my drift).

Grid Tool:
This would be a nice add for people who, like myself, want to make replicas of maps from their favorite game. I have probably failed, 10 time lately trying to make a 10x10 grid on a 10000 Block Map because I'm just bad like that . So! maybe not for the majority of the crowd, but for me this would be a nice add. It doesn't have to be limited to only 10x10 either, for if the numbers vary, making map replicas that for 10x8 or 2x7 and etc, it would make things a lot better.

Invisible Wall Tool:
I recently made a map replica from a game i used to play, and I played Blast/Search-And-Destroy on it countless time. If i do say so my self it is proportionally made correctly and scales nicely with the characters in the game. The only problem is the ability to jump on heads in the game gives people the opportunity to reach parts of the map I wish people would not go. Yes, I could just build parts a bit higher but for me, that would just make things unsatisfactory for me.

My idea for this tool will mainly be useful for finalizing maps to block off parts of a map that people don't want to be exploited, also known as "glitches" in other games. I don't know if people are away of this, and I feel bad for putting this out in the open but players can stack on each others heads to any extent, whether it be double stacking, triple, quadruple, etc. another thing about the walls is they should be able to be shot through, but won't be visible in the map, in addition, will not obscure blocks behind it.

Flying:
This is self explanatory, so I won't go into to great detail of how nice it would be adding the ability to fly while editing simply for the fact that it save more time that building 100m tall blocks.

Texture Tool:
Yes, I did say "Aside from adding extra decorations and color blocks" previously but this is a different approach I thought could be considered. With the Texture Tool I had the idea that, mainly with the NORMAL BLOCKS, that this tool would provide an aging effect to the block. These aging effects could vary in: Rusty, Damaged, Old, Corroded, etc. This could save time from a player having to search for each block with its texture through the inventory. The way of using it, could be by walking up to the object you want textured, and click away. The object would then, switch throughout it's possible various textures until the one the player is satisfied with picks it!

Zoom:
Small idea I had while standing at the very top of a 1x1 tower looking down on a empty 100x100 field. It is somewhat hard on the eyes to pinpoint each square from such a high point, but with zoom (maybe the scroll on the mouse could be used for this) it would make things less tedious. This will probably only be needed, though, the tools mentioned above weren't approved.

Undo/Redo:
Simple idea, but once again, just stating ideas that aren't there yet. Doesn't have to be a tool, but just a key to click to undo what has been done Would be nice if it wasn't limited to only one block as well. So the possibilities are undoing something quick or undoing something you completely regret without having to start a new map or going through the long process of deleting all of it 1 by 1.

Well that concludes a bit of my ideas, unless I'm able to edit later on ill put some more on the table. Thanks for reading!

Snipers are not Over Powered. They have multiple disadvantages which are capable of being used by the players for their advantage.
One useful tool that Brick-Force team has announced is the smoke grenade. It allows the user hide, rendering the snipers aim futile. This is one clear advantage, but is clearly impractical. The cost to use the smoke grenade (not really that important), limited use is the disadvantages of the smoke grenade. The smoke grenade also does not allow the user see through the smoke, thus they are only good for hiding from snipers or heavy attacks.

One major disadvantage that I noticed for a sniper is the fact that they have a low Rate of Fire (RoF)
This creates a window of time for the player to kill the enemy sniper. It requires the player to dodge the sniper's shot. The time between the discharge of ammunition and reload, is enough for a player with a Heavy Machine gun (HMG) or a Sub Machine gun (SMG) to kill the sniper.

Another disadvantage that probably may sniper's have experienced is the fact that snipers are not effective in close range combat. They have no cross-hair, make them not able to aim at the player if they are close. Using the SMG or HMG they can kill a sniper easily.

Both these tactics to go against sniper's come at a risk. If detected before the player got close enough to kill, they might have enough time to react and kill. These are only ideas I thought up, and may not be true in many if not any circumstances.

First, I'd like to say I've been waiting Brick-Force for months and it was really awesome to be accepted in the first wave of invites. I'd like to thank you by writing this feeback, and I hope it will help you to improve this awesome game! =)

--

SHOOTER MODE :

The Shooter Mode is really fun but, apart from the fact it is a world made in cubes, it looks like any other FPS. Sometimes, the game becomes really annoying. Who like to be killed by an headshoot? Who like to be oneshoot by a sniper? Who like be killed 10 times and make only 2 victims? Who like to be killed by an invincible guy??

I love innovatives games that why I'd like Brick-Force to fix all these things.

- First, the game game shouldn't show how many time we died. It isn't really fun to see that we died 15 times in the same game and we only killed 5 ennemies. It isn't fun to put a tag on every player by showing Kill/Deaths %. People are just going to say "Oh, this one is a newbie, he die all the time and he kills almost nobody!".

- Snipers should really be fixed. I mean, they are powerful when we are far, that's normal, but they can also defeat others at melee with their little gun. The second gun shouldn't be allowed for Snipers.

- Headshoots shouldn't kill in one shot. It is really annoying to be one shot by someone just lucky...

- You should really consider reducing the Spawn Protection. I know you can't remove it, because ppl would be killed when they spawn and wouldn't be fun either, but at least you should reduce it because I find it very long!

Again, apart from these 4 bad points, I really enjoy battles in Brick-Force. But if you fix what I said, it would be a perfect and innovating game!

--

SANDBOX MODE :

The Sandbox Mode is just awesome: the blocks are beautiful and the possibilities are infinite. The funniest thing in this game is fighting on our own map, it's really the greatest feature in this game!

- Why don't we have more than 3 maps slots? I guess it takes place on your servers, but let me give you an advice: put some maps slots in the shop. I'd be happy to buy some, even with real money!

- We should have more map edit functions, like editing a Registered Map (without spending all our points again: we should only pay changed blocks), rotating bricks (would open a lot of possibilities), fly (you already know that), and more bricks would also be really awesome!

- You should put something in the shop to delete the Special Bricks limit. I had troubles to finish some maps, like my city, because I didn't have enough Special Bricks to build awesome things!

--

This feedback will be updated every time I have something more to say so, please look again sometimes to see if I updated it. I'm aware that this is only a Closed Beta and there's a lot of things to fix, and it's great for me to help you =)

title: Some bugs and suggestions Wall Spawn bug, Two way teleport, Velocity jumpsl and more.

posts.h:
First of all great game.

I love playing it. For first impressions the combat was quite vanilla but the map making is where I spent most my time. I really enjoy knowing that I can make maps that people will actually play and have fun on. Instead of just looking pretty.

Second: Some bugs I have found.

I made a map with spawn points next to a wall and corner. TBT}Golden sometimes when people spawn they are able to walk through the nearby wall they spawned near I also had a ladder on the outside of the map and the player was able to acess it while inside the block wall, climbing up it.

Recently dropped flags can be grabbed through walls, close to a fence. Have not tested this with plain walls. I believe this is with all the skinny panel walls.

On small maps. 50x50x1 Grayscale. In map editor if people fall off they can respawn and fall off the map again, not landing on the 50x50 ground below.

For general gameplay. I think the Player heads are way too huge, for fps and sniping or any weapon. I notice a lot of people cannot hide even behind a 1x1 square and it is very easy to snipe the large heads.

Third: Suggestions.

I believe the strongest point would be to add more blocks to map editor for people to create things with. Example, more triangle types so they can be able to go on the ceilings or walls. Also if we can save a portion of our map to transfer a 10x10 or 20x20 building to replicate elsewhere on a friends map or copy/pase. Also drag building scaling without having to constantly click my mouse like mad.

A two way teleport block, run into it, go out to the second one would be great for some objectives.

More and customizable objectives.- Instagib (one shot kills), Sniper Only-(for the real big city skyscraper maps) King of the Hill, Oddball, *I see zombies already in some posts* They can obviously be named something else too.

Finally, in my opinion. There should be a jump speed, momentum.. Right now a running jump is a distance 2.5 blocks, I would like it if it was longer only by running longer. so a full run of 2 blocks would grant a 3.5 jump distance instead of a one step jump of 2.5 blocks. -This way I can make really well jumping/bunny track maps.

If you are a TLDR person I highlighted the important parts with an underline.

posts.h:
It just came to me today the idea of having an RPG element into the game of which the use of skills with its corresponding skill tree is. The idea would probably adds twist, excitement, and fun to the game. Here is the mechanics:

Depending on which weapon one uses over time, he / she get to get exp for it in such a way that every level up a point / points is / are gathered to be allocated to enable or increase the level of a particular skill in the skill tree. For example, there's a shotgun-wielder in the game. Throughout one's playtime over time with this weapon, one gets to a point of getting a level with his shotgun skill of which can be used to enable a skill, let's say, a splash shot. The skill gives the player the chance to use the skill at will with only 1 ammo being used. Then there comes the cool-time effect for the next use so as to not abuse the skill amongst players. So basically, as was stated on the first sentence, we're trying to give the game an RPG element to it to give players a chance of a different FPS experience as compared to those existing at its time.

To add some twist to this, there should be a chain reaction between skills of players. Say, we have a shotgun wielder and a AR wielder, both used a certain skill at the same time over a particular player -- a chain reaction amongst the skills used should occur that enhances the overall dmg output of the combined skills. Let's assume in numbers that the dmg output of both skills are at 49, 49 respectively, so that it gives off a total dmg of 49+49=98. But every players in-game has a total HP of 100, so the player has remaining 2 HP left. But with a chain reaction, an additional dmg will be added to the computation to give off a fatal dmg to the player with this simple computation: 49+49+(49/2) = 122.5 = 123 dmg output, a lethal dmg to any player. Chain effects of skills should vary from increase dmg output, to increase range, etc depending on the combo of the skills used; it may even be an AoE effect if the right conditions are met. The dmg output per single player may seem too weak for a skill if one may say, but the idea to do so is to balanced out the gameplay with respect to the skills. By doing so, every player are given a chance for a fair play outside of a player's intrinsic skills in-game.

This may sound DoTA-esque, but yes, that's where the idea come from only embedded in a FPS game instead of the traditional RTS which is the DoTA.

Honestly speaking, I'm not looking forward to seeing this implemented in the game anytime soon as this might become an additional tasks to the developers and the uncertainty of this being acceptable on their part is there. This suggestion might affect the core mechanics of the game which is time-consuming on the part of the developers as well. But it were to be implemented, I'd be the first to get excited about it.

I know. That's we don't see any game of that category in a MMOFPS. It was just a suggestion to begin with. The idea only came to me to encourage team play as we see on DoTA, though not exactly, as the suggestion here isn't equipments / items -oriented but rather giving more emphasis on in-game skills.

the point I'm trying to make is that THIS IS NOT DOTA. We don't need any DOTA style ANYTHING. At this point if you want Team play you go play survival. Or CTF. It's not like there's a giant gap where we're all sitting around going HERP I WISH THIS GAME WAS A MORE RPG.

The map edit is a nice feature to the game that allows you to express your creativity; Ive found both pros and contras, some of which, belonging to the latter could be greatly improved or changed to better the experience of the more large scale creative minds who play the game.

Suggestions for improvement

Testing
  • Currently you can go all out, and edit your map with as much freedome as possible. Once you've finished though, there is no way to test your map to see if it will be any good with all it's elements (turret placement, fall dmg potential..etc), without having to spend nearly all your points (depending on scale) in order to test it. Ive checked all options and there doesnt seem to be a mode to test that I know of. Implementing a feature that allowed you make a mock battle with all those present (solo aswell), so we can test the way it would work in a real battle without having to spend excess points.

Registering
  • What uses up your points I have come to understand. It appears to be 1 point per normal block, and 10 per special(?). Fair game, but, what happens when I wish to make an edit to my map? Make a spawn change or fix an imbalance? I surely dont want the old map still in circulation! Implementing a way to use either 1/3 of the original point registration requirement, or none at all, to updade your map should be actively explored. It would be similar to save, except, it will update your published/registered map, if it bares the same name.

Flying
  • The bigger your project, the more room for flexability you're going to want to finish it. It could work similar to walking, but the direction you are aiming in when you're pressing forward, is where you go (think swimming). Also, backwards as well obviously. Because making 40-story block poles isnt always such a quick deal.

Block Rotations
  • Some blocks, namely the triangular ramp ones, would be best used to express better art if they were able to be turned upside down. I have a hypothesis that if you jump from a high area and some how manage to turn upside down as you are about to shoot the blo-...no. Wouldnt work. How about a way to switch any and all blocks' orientation? (eg. The little siren lights: they only seem to ever be facing upright. Why dont they have their base on the surface of the block you place them on despite its direction?) Having an object rotating feature ofcourse, would fix this problem for the most part.

Map Saving (Question/suggestion)
  • When this game eventually goes into open beta or full term, will there be a way to still attain your map projects? If not, I'd strongly suggest a way to make either the players save their work on their local HD, or it is saved on the servers along with general account information such as name and other saved information.

Over all, extremely fun game. I dont know what im going to do once classes start again. I may have to call in and have my internet connection suspended. If im not playing a map with other players, Im working on a new idea for a map, which arent 1 day endeavours.

I noticed today when I logged in today that I now had access to something called 'Luck'.

Now from what I can gather, and please correct me if I'm wrong, 'Luck' is the equivalent of a dodge chance. This mechanic in a FPS is odd to say the least for the simple reason gunplay will now have a luck factor. There is a chance, for example I could land three headshots and do no damage because someone was lucky, which is of course is just silly, and in a way it seriously devalues your product.

But this aside, the real issue is that 'Luck' can only be acquired through tokens, which again correct me if I'm wrong, can only be purchased with real cash. If everything I have said so far is correct then you have just taken your game into the realms of 'pay-2-win' a place where not many gamers like to venture. This is a risk because you are gambling the possible profits from 'luck' against those who do not like to 'pay-2-win' and in a game like this, which will try to compete in a market saturated by similar products, you may cripple your potential audience.

Let me offer a constructive alternative; why not have 'luck' represent the chance that when you kill an enemy, that person will follow one of any pre-set death animations. For example, if I land a neat headshot with the revolver maybe that head will literally explode into lots of smaller bricks in an exciting way! Or you could have people being killed by machine guns have their limbs fly of their torso. Both cosmetic, both ethical, and both awesome.

A second alternative is have luck a much smaller percent; for example have luck at around 0.1% then have it so for every kill you get in game, or the difference between your kills and deaths, multiplies this luck value so at the end of the round you may have something like 2.7% luck. Then you could have a 2.7% to win a random gun for a period of time, at the end of the round. This way you can still 'sell' the value, it's not 'pay-2-win' and it still matters.

That way you not only add new features to the game, but it also gives 'Luck' some actual value rather than just an arbitrary dodge chance. Of course please excuse me if I'm completely of target! But If I'm right on the money then I offer this as my personal opinion based on what myself and others I play with feel.

Youtube Channel
An ingame recorder would be handy, As it'd likely be capturing raw data for the sound as well, And not everyone has a soundboard with the speaker recording mixer.

Personally I don't like the idea. You do realize that Fraps video is like 1.5GB/5min video, and that is not even uncompressed. It would make far more sense just to add a demo record function like most other FPS games. If you want to put anything on youtube then you could view the demo and record that way. It also is better for frames since recording video takes a lot of CPU power but if it was just a demo the frames don't matter since you're not playing. Also, say you wanted to make a highlight reel. You would need countless GB's of video just to have enough for a full reel, but with demos you only need to record the specific parts you want.

One reason why there's a cost to register is to try and bring down XP maps. I'm sure you've seen and maybe even played in one, and it costs what seems like a pointless amount of money to make, especially considering how many other XP maps there are. There's a minimum and maximum price so that people can't just shrink an xp map to 16 blocks. Another problem with free-registering maps is...actually I don't know anything other than that o_o. At least there's a maximum price for if you're making something crazy awesome.

As for special block limits, I agree with JohnCreed, it does make sense with laggy blocks like fire and game changers like turrets. What I don't understand is how small some limits are on simple blocks, like steel pillars (those tiny sideways rectangles), anti-turret barricades, sandbags, and most of all glass and wood crates.

title: Isn't "Build and destroy" kinda lacking something?

posts.h:
Honestly, as it stands right now build and destroy is really lacking something. There's just one problem with this game type actually. Predictability. Everyone does the same thing each time.

If you've ever played a match against good players you know only one strategy is being currently applied. Everyone who plays the mode will always builds a wall/trench to keep out the other side from entering and then proceeds to make one huge ass sniper tower. I mean, everyone does this and they do it for a reason. Walls and sniper towers are the most effective strategy, but I can't help but feel like this isn't how this game type was intended to be played. I imagined people building mazes, forts, and all kind of cool ****, but not this every time.

Naturally though, there would be one easy way to fix the wall/trench strategy everyone does. Well, not easy, but effective to say the least.

Make the floor out of destructible blocks, and make it where we can actually destroy regular blocks during the building phase. I mean, you obviously don't want them too destructible, otherwise the playing field would be leveled each round. I'm talking about just conventional enough that someone can dig their way out of a trench or break a hole in the wall so the other team can't camp on their side. I suppose you could make it where each person can only break like four or six blocks each destroy round. Give them limited breaking ability.

Now on the second problem. Sniper towers. Personally I hate these things with a passion. Cause I don't wanna have to use a certain gun just to play a certain mode. Anyone not using snipers during build and destroy are basically dead weight. To destroy the usefulness of sniper towers one could easily do many things. Maybe create a pre-built roof every so many feet? Give an option for a roof, or hell. Maybe a nice preset two thick glass wall in the center of the map that is up to the sky limit. Something that would stop snipers from covering the entire map unless they wanna waste their entire ammo supply and three minutes tearing it down.

Honestly though, I would really like a destroying option implemented more so than anything else. It would really fit the name well, and it would help get rid of the most annoying part of the game type. Although it's just an idea. And if anything I've gave you guys some ideas on it, I'll be glad.

title: Why use Unity? Suggestions for improvement.

posts.h:
Of all game engines that would prove to be a million times more suitable for a game like this, why go with Unity? I noticed it wasn't a registered/published Unity build on the Unity site, so I'm guessing the developers weren't using a commercial license for the game and that's why it's free-to-play with the exception of the item store.

I've yet to see ONE successful Unity game, and believe me I know Unity... I work with it as a profession at Cartoon Network Games; where all game's produced are Unity-based and make use of Unity Web Player (a total abomination). All day I see nothing but people complaining about frame-rate lag due to the high processor resource budget required by Unity-based games (it's even worse when streaming assets via Unity Web Player).

The "Graphics" adjuster is not only backwards, but it only decreased texture quality. Generally when an adjuster just says "Graphics" is also swaps all models with lower poly LOD models, but I don't even think LOD's were used in Brick-Force which would severely improve the performance of the game for all users.

A shaders expert should have been hired early on in development to create custom shaders that more successfully achieve the desired look of Brick-Force with a lower processor resource budget cost. The current faux "toon shading" prefab, that comes default with Unity, requires all clients to render all models TWICE, one sized slightly more than the original with inverted normals and a black texture, just to achieve a visually lacking, faux "render edge". With already obscenely high-poly weapons and some accesories, rendering them twice is melting GPU's world-wide.

The ladder detection is poor, I find myself and others constantly falling off ladders trying to climb them (ultimately penalizing themselves with a "self-inflicted death"), getting stuck on ladders when going moving up or down through a 1 x 1 x 1 block-sized hole, and when trying to move side to side to get on platforms located along the sides of ladders.

posts.h:
Topics:

1. Build Stuff

1.1: Gravity system.
- It's a simple concept. Create a "gravity editor" for the map building !
Why? Imagine you playing a space themed (Example: Planet Mars or even the Moon) map with tall structures... Now imagine you jumping 2-3x times higher than before ! I really need to say more?

- Make maps with bigger or lower gravity... there's not much sandbox around with this concept ! (is there?)

1.2: Moving plataforms/Elevators.
- Imagine a flying moving plataform that can take you to the other side without any rush. Like a boss.

- Elevators? Why make giants structures if it take years to get on the higher floors? It will make the game flow better !

1.3: Interactive bricks( doors/buttons ).
- Imagine metallic doors that open if you press a small button. It will make some structures looks better and will add more strategy for the shooter mode ! ( defusion for example )

1.4: Map of the week "prize".
- Creating a sort of "prize" for map of the week, will make people aim for constructing more EPIC maps ! And we surely want to see this creations often !

- What kind of prize it could be? Well... more maps slots? Tokens? Rare gear?

- Giving more map slots, will encourage the person to keep up the work.

1.5: Your own soundtrack.
- Make possible the use of BGMs for maps !

1.6: Your background.
- Make possible the creation of your own "sky background"

- Like color, clouds, stars, moons, suns, planets.

2. Brick Points

2.1: Buy map slots.
- We know that actually we're limited to only 3 maps slots ( 5 for premium ) and that brick points are only used for register maps and stuff like that.

- Why not make more slots buyable via brick points? ( if not, we just have to make another account and use the 3 extra slots... but that sucks. )

- Example: First buyable slot price = 20k, second buyable slot price = 25k, third = 30k.... etc

- A real good utility for brick points.

2.2: Special itens for "Clan War System"
- Make a shop with special itens that can help on strategies for the "CWS".

- Example: A heartbeat minetrap. When an enemy pass over it, his heartbeat will appear on your radar for a little time.

- Example of shop: 100 heartbeat minetraps = 500 Brick Points/ 50 Tokens.

- It will make a brick points based shop that is essencial for end-game players.

3. Clan War System

3.1: Clan interaction and endgame.
- The CWS will happen once a week at the sartuday at 12:00AM ( random hour).

- Veteran players will focus on getting essencial "usables" ( brick point shop enter here ;D) for the CWS.

- This will make even the veteran players don't get bored of the game ! And will be fun like hell !

3.2: The CWS.
- The concept i have for the CWS is a "King of the hill" or a "protect the golden brick" stuff.

- It will be a special room where multiple players can join and spectate. Once the first clan reach the "protection spot" the clan will have to protect it from all the other clans one by one.

- Well, i have to kind of goals in my mind:
First = the clan that hold the protection spot on the end of the war wins.

Second = the clan that holds the spot for more time. Example: xPROx held it for 37 minutes. Alt - F4 held it for 20 minutes. xPROx Win.

- It's an early concept, but i think it has some potential.

3.2: The fun and the treasure.
- Why waste your time getting usables for the CWS?

First = Fun time with the clan and the community.

Second = Who won will have the right to play an especial "defense mode" with 10 waves of "treasure-bees".

- Each treasure-bee will have the chance to drop special itens and rare gear ( that can only be obtained with treasure-bees" )

- So now we have a system of work-goal-fun-prize. Now Clans have a REAL purpose !

4. Beginner/Veteran BALANCE

4.1: The actual Brick-Force unbalance problem.
- The new players just got scared when they play the first matches.

- Why? They just see the big PLAY button and ignore the "beginners" button... So they face veteran players like me and are massacred. Nobody wants to play a game where you die all the time ! There's no fun on death. So they just quit the game.

- Gems... with the upgrade system, the veteran players got even more advantage ! Newbies don't have enough force points to buy gems and better weapons on the beginning.

- First of all, make a block for the "normal play server" !

- Rage-quit will be drastically lowered and the community will grow.

- Make some bosses for defense mode.

- Make rank count when facing bosses ( more ranked you are, more stronger the boss is )

- Challenge your players ! We need goals for continue playing a game !

- When you're hosting a room and you want to start the game, probably there will be some guy on shop or equiping... but you can't even make a count for him get ready.... because he can't read while shopping/equipping ! So we just kick him :/

title: Rank point balance No option team balance excluding locked servers No xp boost maps

posts.h:
Rank point balance

The basic Idea here is to give every rank a certain point balance. Example being Lowest = 20 points Highest = 50 points. Lowest would have to start with at least a few points otherwise a team gaining a lower level member would have no chance of changing the point balance before the next player came in
We've all seen the servers. Almost every other match you have a team filled with low levels and the other team filled with high levels sitting on their spawn wiping them out with the inexperienced having no chance to do anything hardly.
Why not make it so that no balanced team can have SO much more experience or rank stacked than the other by setting a maximum distance between the point totals of each team?

No option team balance

It's basically this. As soon as a team starts doing bad, through the leaving and rejoining process, 1 team often ends up getting messed up bad with 8 v 4s or so for the whole rest of the game even with new joiners, who out of desire to join the winning team for extra XP, of course join the team with the ton of people on it destroying the little guys. Anyway, enough babble, what I am trying to get at here is that any server created for public should not even have a checkbox for the creator to chose to make it balanced or not. It should just be built right in for any unlocked server. These are public servers made to have fun in, not for clan folk or people in online calls who join together to go in and clean house on XP and FP. If they happen to get on the same team, good for them, but it should not be their option in a open server.

Getting rid of XP booster maps

I found myself in one of these maps recently and IMMEDIATELY realized that this was the ultimate form of not playing the game for the game, but rather for prestige.
Anyway, a thought to get rid of the XP booster maps. Very simple in the eyes of a non programmer. No idea how this would be to program in. Anyway, each team's spawns must have a minimum distance between them such as perhaps 25 or 30 meters or something like that. OR make it so that in the case of indoor maps or C shaped maps, a spawn point must have no line of sight to another enemy spawn point anywhere within a certain radius from the point. This would allow spawn points under the minimum distance to be able to be placed so long as there was sufficient LOS barriers in place to not allow for spawn to spawn killing. Though it may not COMPLETELY eliminate spawn killing, it would at least make it more difficult to create these types of maps.
Also, banning the use of the words XP, map, boost, booster, etc, from being used together in the map titles is always a great way to start along with occasionally checking for new maps using words such as bstr and Xperinen3 and other words they will purposely misspell to get the map's purpose across as it being a booster map and adding those misspelled words to the ban list.

Maybe someone should reply with a full concept of how a vote kicking system could work:

-You can only vote in the lobby, and anyone can start a vote.
-If the majority or half vote to kick, the person subject to the vote is kicked. If the majority vote not to kick or less than 1/4 of the room votes, then the person is here to stay.
-Room leaders are automatically kicked if everyone is ready and 30 seconds have passed. A new leader is then voted on. New leaders are chosen by a majority as first priority, but if any one ties in number of votes, the leader will be picked randomly from the people who tied. That means if two people tie in number of votes, then one is picked randomly. If no one votes for anyone, then the leader is picked randomly from everyone.
-You may not vote to kick yourself or vote for yourself as room leader.
-A votekick will last for 20 seconds and will stop the all-ready room leader timer, and a room leader vote will last for 10 seconds.
-You may not vote to kick someone more than once until a round in the game has ended.
-If you leave during a votekick you started, the vote ends.
-You do not have to vote.
-You must pay 150 FP to initiate a votekick. You can receive back your money if the vote is successful.

If there's any details I missed, I will gladly edit them in/change current details.
And you have to pay 150 for vote kicks. Cuts down on uneeded vote kicks.

All of the melee weapons look pretty much the same in stats, only most of the bought ones give an insta-kill. Wouldn't it be cooler if they were more diverse instead of just dealing more damage and looking cooler? For example, you could change the distance of its reach or how fast it swings, or maybe give it special effects (I can imagine people swinging torches and lighting each other on fire =P). The melee weapons in this game are hardly used for anything except to kill afk players or as a last resort (that usually fails). If they took a larger, creative role in gameplay, people could do more than just shoot, shoot, shoot. For example:

Bat: Deals 30% damage with longer range and faster swing.

Bayonet: Attaches to your main weapon for faster melee attacks (pressing 3 switches to your main weapon if you aren't equipping it, otherwise no time to change to melee)

Torch: Sets people on fire! Not a lot of base melee damage though.

Glowstick: I know there's a glowing billy club, but this weapon breaks on hitting an enemy, is throwable, and makes the enemy much more visible with all the glowy stuff on him/her. Very little damage though.

Rubber Ducky: Very low damage, but can either confuse the opponent by spinning them around, or gives more money on a kill.

Drill: A modified drill tool, deals very little damage but dishes it out rapidly.

Buzzsaw: Like the drill, it doesn't go as fast but breaks glass and other fragile bricks instantly.

Glass Block: It's literally a glass block! Smash it on an enemy to lose the weapon until your next life, but the shards that fly off deal damage to surrounding foes. Of course, no one said you couldn't just place the block down as a barrier =P.

Boomerang: A low damage melee weapon that can be thrown and bounced off random objects/people before it magically runs the same path backwards. It can't be picked up again, however, and it can actually hurt the user if he/she's in the way!

Stunstick: A special billy club with no damage, but can slow players and make it harder for them to turn.

Fist: Your hand swings fast, but slightly shorter range and less damage than the wrench. At least you don't have to repair it...

Hammer: Slower than a wrench, but it instantly kills and has quite the range. The player slows down somewhat while holding the Hammer, but the weight allows players to kill by jumping on people's heads!

Flail: A slow, powerful weapon that can be swung to a distance of 3 blocks. It's very hard to control the spiked end, however.

Climbing Hook: Very short range, average swing speed, low damage. Using it in front of a block lets you climb at 3/4th the speed of climbing ladders.

Helmet: Land a hit on an opponent's head and they won't be able to see for five seconds! You can't really dish out a lot of damage with a helmet though, and you also lose a perfectly good helmet on a 'headshot'...

Defective Grenade: The default grenade, only defective and less range than a wrench. However, it only failed once in combat so no one really knows what it could do on impact...

Brick-Wrench: A special combat wrench that has no damage, 2 second swing rate, but longer range. Its specialty is making blocks temporarily disappear for 2 seconds! They appear as brick ghosts, the ones you see while a block is being placed. Blocks won't revert to normal if a person is standing in them. It also only works on non-special bricks.

Defibrillator: Hard to lug around on your back, but it has a small chance of reviving any dead body on a hit, whether it be enemy or friendly! The person returns with 50% hp and no armor, but half ammo regardless of if they had a lot or none previously. Its weight makes it harder to swing, but it has a longer and wider range.

Giant Shuriken: A big ninja star with a pretty fast swing speed and very low reach. Right click throws it forward at the speed of throwing a grenade, dealing 60 damage to each target struck. Did I mention the star can penetrate through enemies? [Note: You can't recover shuriken until next life]

Originally Posted by Shinji
The repair costs were changed as follows.
You have a main weapon, a pistol, a wrench, and a grenade.

If you then only use the main weapon and the grenade, only those will decay.

That is, if you only press the 1 and 4 keys to switch to them, then your pistol and wrench will not decay.
However, if you scroll through with your mouse wheel, they will.

The decay works as follows:

Each minute, a weapon will decay by 0.5%, which costs 10 FP to repair.
A 10 minute match means a decay of 5%, and 100 FP repair costs.

Thus, a weapon can cost a maximum of 2000 FP to repair.

title: Remove the "clear expired items" button, or make it idiot-proof

posts.h:
In the inventory, there's a button that does what its tooltip says: It deletes all expired/depleted items from your inventory.

This is kinda dangerous nowadays for one simple reason: Expired items retain upgrades, and when you re-buy them, they'll still be there. If you accidentally press that button and delete your expired rentals, you lose the upgrades on them forever.

There really is no need to delete expired items anyway, unless you buy clothes/accessories purely for actual fashion value and don't upgrade them at all. A few suggestions to make this a bit safer:

  • Remove the button entirely. I mean, when is your inventory ever so cluttered that cleaning it up one by one becomes tedious?
  • Give it an additional confirmation dialog, à la "Are you sure you want to delete (number of) expired items? Yes/No".
  • Make it not delete expired items that have upgrades on them. Those could still be deleted individually.

Also, while we're at it, the delete button on single items could also use an "are you sure?" prompt if it has upgrades on it.
posts.t: Remove the "clear expired items" button, or make it idiot-proof

title: F2P (Free to Play) games: What people don't understand...

posts.h:
...that I happen to have a bit more of an understanding of.
I have a online friend who's uncle used to work for a company who hosts one of these types of games and, by the looks of posts lately, I don't think people quite understand how F2P works.
F2P Basics:
Here's what I have gotten from his rants at least as far as it makes sense to me. The same things that happen in the forums here, happens everywhere else. People want everything to be this "permanent" word that everyone keeps bringing up in the forums. "oh why can't this or that be permanent it would help us a lot". By the time you look through the forums, everyone has given a reason why almost EVERY feature in the game should, in their mind, be permanent. However there is a huge problem with that. Making something permanent to your account means one thing. They can no longer make money from that feature. The makers of these games can't AFFORD for it to be easier for "you". If you want it to be easy for you then shuck out $60, get your advanced pack with instant LVL 5 or 10 and what-not and the instant unlocked weapons, but that is simply not how it works in F2P games because hey, these guys gotta pay the bills too ya know. That is why these types of posts are pretty much 100% futile. They will make permanent what they can make permanent and that will be that.
Pay-To-Win
Pay-to-win. People complain tirelessly on any F2P forum about the people who they call "pay-to-win". Sure go ahead and call them a noob ingame, BUT, you free to play folk out there are not the ones who keep the game alive and funded. These people that actually throw money into this game are what is keeping you playing this game. Sure you may end up taking a beating from some guy who is pay-to-win, but guess what, think of it as he just bought the game for you. Don't go onto the forums and cry about it and try and say that we should all be as equals because those people that pay for your game most certainly should not be equals. they SHOULD be well ahead of you. If I payed a monthly fee or ANY sort of fee that not all others had to pay I gotta say I darn well BETTER be kicking butt with what I got or man I must suck. People out there are just going to have to accept the facts. You can either accept that pay to win will always win, (unless they truly suck) and that there is nothing, and never will be anything that will change that in any F2P game.

Also note I posted in Constructive feedback because this is where people seem to make these types of posts as I thought that would make it on the topic.

If I then decide to switch it up by equipping the Scarab (which is a light weapon), I have to remember to buy and equip the "light" ammo refill instead. If I forget to do this, I'm stuck having to kill myself to get my ammo back.

Another thing: If you join a pistol match, you have to remember to switch to a pistol refill beforehand, every single time, because you get so little ammo otherwise. And of course you gotta remember to switch back afterwards.

This is annoying. I have a solution, though: When you drag a light/medium/heavy/long refill item to your Action Panel, it doesn't become that item. Instead, it becomes a generic "main refill" button that changes automatically depending on the match type, and what you have equipped.

  • If you equip a light weapon, it becomes a light ammo refill.
  • If you equip a medium weapon, it becomes a medium ammo refill. (etc.)
  • In a pistol match, it automatically becomes a pistol refill.
  • In a melee match, it is unusable.

You would still have to buy all the consumables separately, but basically you'd automatically equip whatever refill type makes sense in that situation. Having an assault rifle refill makes no sense when you're sniping - having to manually change it is just unnecessary.
posts.t: Add a generic "main weapon refill" to the Action Panel

DON'T BE AFRAID OF READING A LONG POST.

Ok, heres my Card Game idea for Brick-Force. It's a sidegame. Played on your account on the website? In-Game? Both?.. I'm not sure, but here we go!

::The Basics::

:1. The Goal:
There's a basic goal in this game.

K.O. 10 to 15 (Settable) enemy cards.

In this order, this is ressemblance to Team Deathmatch, get to the score limit first to win.

Or, be in the lead when the number of rounds end.

You can have a total of 20 Battle Cards, 25 Weapon Cards (Main) and 10 Weapon Cards (Secondary), 10 Upgrade Cards, and 10 Medical Cards.
A total of 75 Cards.

:2. Cards:


2.1 Battle Cards:

The main cards of the game.
Unlike traditional "Fire, Beast" types, these cards have mastery in different weapons, such as Snipers or Assualt Rifles Masteries.

2.1.2: A Basic Battle Card:



1: Name of the Card

2: Level (Used for Special Purposes)

3: Health (When this hits 0, The Card has been K.O'ed.)

3.1: Maximum Health Limit

4: Armour

4.1: Maximum Armour limit

5: Weapon Icon (Shows what type of weapon can be equiped to this card)

6: Speed

NOTE: Unlike the traditional "P1 Attacks, Turn ends, then P2 Attacks, turn ends" type of Card Gameplay, Speed is used to determine which Card attacks first. The Card with the higher speed attacks first, regardless of turn.

7: Rank (Value)

2.2: Weapon Cards

These are vital as Battle Cards, without these you can't attack.
Battle Cards have their own respective mastery of weapon types, meaning one that uses a SMG, can't use a Sniper.
However, every Card can use Pistols.

There are Five types of Weapons;

(Main) Snipers

(Main) Assualt Rifles

(Main) Sub-Machine guns

(Main) Light-Machine Guns

(Secondary) Pistols

(Special) Weapons with abilities

2.2.1: Main Weapons

Main weapons are, well, the main weapon.
The Main Weapon is used for directly attacking an enemy.

Also, if you run out of Weapon Cards to use, you lose. Use your weapons effeciently.


2.2.2: Secondaries

When you are attacked, you cannot counter attack with your main weapon.
But if you get attacked while having a Pistol also equiped, although you'll take the damage first, and if you don't get K.O'ed, your pistol will deal damage to your attacker.

NOTE: If the card with the same Stats, Weapons, etc has targeted each other, the player who goes first, attacks first.


2.2.3: Specials

What specials do is, they do something different then regular weapons.

Think of flashbangs, they blind the enemy.

Grenades, they can K.O and damage multiple enemies.

However, note that they must be equiped to a Battle Card to be used. And also:

They are treated like Main Weapons, meaning that if you have a card with a Special Weapon equiped, you cannot use your Main weapon if you choose to use your Special Weapon.

Most Specials can only be used once.

2.2.3: Card Stats


1: Weapon Name

2: Weapon Type

3: Damage Per Use (DPU)

4: Durability / Number of uses (When this hits 0, the Weapon is no Longer usable and must be discarded.)

5: Weight (Lowers Speed)


2.3: Medical Cards

Used to give health to the selected battle card.

NOTE: i) Some Battle Cards may start with less then 100 Health.

ii) Medical Cards can't pass (Or possibly Overheal) the Limit Health.

iii) Some battle Cards may start with Armour, however like health, they have a limit.

2.4: Armour Cards

Used to give the Battle Card "Extra" health.

There are 4 Categories for Armour: Helmet, Topwear, Bottomwear, and Footwear.

Once an Armour has been added to a Battle Card, no more Armour can be can be equipped for that category.
(For example. If you give a Card a "Shirt" (Topwear), you can no longer equip Topwear Armours to that card.)

NOTE: If a card loses all of its Armour, even if it just equipped one piece of Armour, it can no longer equip Armours.

Some Armours have special abilities. (Such as: +5 Speed, or such.)

If the Armour equipped passes the Maximum Armour Limit, then only the limit will be counted as the current health for the Armour.
(No Extra Armour.)


2.5: Upgrades Cards

Things that increase (and sometimes decrease as a price) the status of a Weapon card.

Some are Weapon Type specific.
Some are Level specific.

Also, a weapon can only be upgraded 3 times.


:3. The Game Field:


3.1: Field Info

1: Player Name

2: Battle Card Pad (Battle Cards are placed here, maximum of 5 Pads.)

3: Hospital (K.O'ed Battle Cards)

4: Junkyard (Broken Weapons and used Medical Items)

5: Round Count (2 Turns count as a Round)

6: Score

:4: The Game Flow:

The game goes on about 7 Phases, as 1 Turn.

A coin flip will begin at the start of the game.

If Heads, the Challenger starts first.
If Tails, the Defender starts first.

4.1: Phases


4.1.1: Send-in Phase [SP]

In this one, you pick one, or more battle cards from your Card Base.
Instead of the traditional "Deck" system, in this one you pick your cards.

NOTE: However, not all cards can be put in at the same time.

Rounds determine what-to-what levels can be sended in.

Meaning, that you can't basically send in a Level 65 Battle Card in the First Turn.
(Unless a custom option is set in.)

CHART OF ROUNDS AND LEVELS
Round 1: Levels 1-5

Round 2: Levels 1-15

Round 3: Levels 1-25

Round 4: Levels 1-35

Round 5: Levels 1-45

Round 6: Levels 1-55

Round 7: Levels 1-65

4.1.2: Gear-Up Phase [GP]

In this phase, you equip weapons to your Battle Cards, and if needed, use Medical Cards and Upgrades.


4.1.3: End Phase [EP]

The end of your turn.
After this it's your enemies turn. (If you went first)

NOTE: Your enemy cannot see what actions you have done in the phases.


4.1.4: War Phase [WP]

This phase is where it gets to the battle. You don't fight yet, but you pick who attacks who.


4.2: Battle

When you and your enemy are done with your selections, it's time to fight.

The one with the most speed, goes first!

Like I said, no "You attack first, then I do" here.


4.3: Results

Who took how much damage?
Who got K.O'ed?
What Broke?

The results are in, in this.

Who gets K.O'ed, goes to the 'Hospital,.

What Broke goes to the 'Junkyard,.

The ones who aren't down yet, stay on the field.

After this phase, it's an end of a Round.

Then the next Round begins.

Until the game ends, (Score limit has been reached, or a number of Rounds has been reached) this keeps on going.

2.6: Action Cards

Cards that have abilities at certain moments.

For example: Action Card: "Spawn Shield"


Used in: Battle Phase, when attacked.
Ability: Block

If the card has been send-in this Round. And is attacked. This card makes the Battle Card take no damage for that attack.

After an Action has been used. It is discarded to the 'Junkyard,.

NOTE: Action Cards have these Abilities:
*Block (Makes you take no damage)

*Reload (Makes you be able to attack twice. Sometimes with a negative side.)

*Dodge (Works only if you have more speed then your attacker. If you have more speed, then you take 0 Damage.)

*Grind (Take half of the damage taken.)

*Hack (Negate the effects of a Certain, or Certain Type of Action Card from the Enemies side which is activated.)

+5 Speed, +5 Damage for Snipers

-5 Speed, -5 Damage for Snipers

title: Isn't it about time the average Force Points income took a hike?

posts.h:
It was terrible the whole time, really. Everything was, and still is, completely overpriced, meaning that only the rich people could afford anything. title: A realistic solution to the "Armor Problem."

posts.h:
For those who seem to complain about armor I do see where you are coming from. I recently took a little trip to the EU server ( where I intend to spend my mornings for the next two weeks in Melee-only matches ) and realized I couldn't compete very well unless I managed to lure my opponents into small spaces and then spray at their heads from behind, which left me with a pistol to finish off the kill. I realized that if you want to win without armor, you need to play in Melee Matches or be ready to preform a lot of sneak attacks.

I recently thought of two realistic solutions however. It is my hope that these two solutions will gain the support of the player base and Infernum's community team. Below are the two fixes.

A: Change the armor system so it does not stop Brick-Shots if it does: A Brick-Shot should be a Brick-Shot and I feel armor should NOT stop a Brick-Shot if armor is currently programmed to do so.

B: If you look at other games that start you out with armor, the average seems to be 100. The power of these guns seems to be in the 30-40 power range, and I feel that weapons in Brick-Force should hold 30-50 power on average in order to balance out the armor currently in existence. I know this leaves players with armor wondering about how their advantage will stay an advantage and it is really simple. Infernum could add a "Health Shelf" which would have five shelves, the top three with first-aid kits and the bottom area with two bullet proof vests taking up two shelf sizes ) and when a player stood next to it for 10 seconds it would restore 20 armor points and 20 health. This would balance it out I feel, and would love to hear your thoughts on my idea.

Alright. The US server has been plagued with enough problems as it is. Hackers, xp farms galore, but I'm not here to complain about them, I'm here to complain about the problem I think Brick-force can fix.

Problem: 1 vs 8
The last thing we really need is idiots constantly setting up 1 versus 8 matches just in hopes for easy xp, points, and a good kill to death ratio. It trolls a lot of people's time here, whether or not you're a long time member or a new guy. It's nearly impossible to win against the one guy, no matter how good you are, mainly cause noobs will always feed him more than you can kill him. The noobs don't even know they're feeding him, and they just end up leaving after giving him 40 kills or so. These matches aren't fair and they need to go. The only people who enjoy them are that 1 guy out of 8, and only cause he realizes how cheap it is too. If you've ever been stuck in one of those matches you'd realize straight off just how cheap it is, and why it needs to go.

Solution: auto-balance
Auto-balance. I know what you're gonna say, we already have auto-balance, and they just end up turning it off. Well, here is one easy way to solve the problem. Forcibly enact auto-balance until the room is half full or so, or at least the same princible. Have auto-balance turn off after a decent amount of players are on both sides. Too avoid situations like 1 vs 8, and to put a halt to these annoyingly cheap tactics. I can understand Infernum wants to give players a choice in the matter, but at this point waaaaaay too many people are abusing this feature, it needs to go or be nerfed to a point where they can't abuse it.

See, a nessesary auto ballance would not work too well for some people. I for one, hate it. I never have it on. When I do it messes up teams. Example: Clan vs Clan. You have a couple of spots open for other clan mates, and then it's auto balance, and you have the teams messed up... So, we need something to change. Just nothing to annoy anyone.

Some issues with build mode and simple fixes.
A lot of the blocks people like to use are the special blocks. I tried making a city type map called "Rush-Hour". Although people love the map, I had to substitute car tires with 1/4 blocks because there is a 50 item limit. That is only 12 1/2 cars, assuming the cars only had 4 tires and I didn't want to make semi-trucks... Thats just one example. Another would be glass blocks. Another build issue is lack of constructive blocks. If you have a full block, ex: a red block, you should have a half block with it. every square block should have it's half doppleganger so that you can properly construct ramps and roofs etc...

Light weapons are meant to be crowd control up close and personal quick protection with spray and pray. They generally have very little damage and extremely erratic bullet path behavoir.
Medium weapons ie: M16 type of weapons are generally semi-fully automatic weapons. normally great power, decent accuracy and lower rate of fire.

Explain why it's not fair and offer a viable solution? Challenge accepted. Plus, I'll try my hardest to not mention pay2win for this post only. Fair?

Every tier of weapon has a pretty big boost to the next one in terms of most all stats. This is common in a lot of MMOs, free to play or not. The problem here is that these tiers share the same gameplay space and have a very big difference between them. This means that higher tiers (aka payers and veterans) will be getting the majority of their easy kills off lower tiers, and lower tiers won't be able to progress without having to go through a bunch of deaths. This would be considered no fun to a lot of players, making them leave.

So, lower tiers will be sitting through, watching dozens of players with their powerful weapons laugh at them.
Higher tiers will be going through what is essentially a single player CoD mission since the servers are populated with low tiers going in and out of the game.
Both tiers tend to have more fun when they're matched with their own starred weapons.

I didn't want to propose my solutions mainly because it would be rather unbelievable and probably not a change a lot of players would like, although it would solve the problem for the newbies cycling in and out with their bad reviews ready. Note that each idea listed is separate, and I do not recommend employing them all at once.

1. Set up servers that require certain tiers of guns. For example, Tier 2 server would allow both tier 1 and 2 (this idea could be tested with the beginner's server). Tier 4 server would allow tiers one, two, three, and four. The free server would allow all weapons. This would be hard to put in, though, as it would be difficult to get the populations of each up and going without a big playerbase. Would be nice to see what would happen in Europe with this.

2. Do a major re-haul of every weapon in the game, and give each a more unique feel. All of the automatic guns feel like a boost from each other, and making them more balanced and giving each certain boosts/downgrades unique to the weapon would make an instant balance. Guns that require more skill to use but do better with said skill should have a greater price tag.

3. Add more creative guns to the game, and make them available to all with ease. Sub-weapons are hardly used, so why not put something special, like a temporary frontal shield, grapple hooks, and cloaks, among other things? Surely the shield would work with the Brick-Star theme.

Also, this is a little off-topic, but Bomberer is simply young and unaware of internet etiquette (hah. like that exists =P). Instead of telling him he's an eleven year old nooby selfish idiot, you should respond as you would to others. He apologized once too, yet you still treated him with hostility. Although respect isn't necessary for something as lawless as the internet, it still gets you pretty far in some places.

"If they want realistic help GREAT, if not, dig that grave. (probably only 3x1 blocks) I'll even make a nice graveyard map if they want."

That part made me literally laugh, good one haha!

But humour aside, I completely agree. This is a serious matter, or rather matters that Infernum should take care of.

Infernum is smart to say the least. They know their ways of gaining money. Problem is though, their whole game is based on paying. Take the 2D side-scroller MapleStory for example. I know about this game, trust me. I played it 6 years. Anyway, Nexon who is in charge of MapleStory started small. You only had to pay real money if you wanted good character customization such as looks. Later on, over the years, you had to get real money if you wanted to get more in-game money for better equipment. Brick-Force launched and BOOM--already the whole game is based on paying real money. Now, what I'm actually trying to say is, even though in MapleStory you need to pay real money if you want more in-game money for better weapons and equipment, that doesn't interfere with the core gameplay. Why? Well, you don't need very strong weapons or armour if you want to train on monsters and do quests. You care about better equipment if you want to go bossing with other players pretty much. Now compare this as opposed to Brick-Force, where using real money IS the game.

Hopefully I made my point of comparison explaining about how far Infernum should go with making players use real money.

Woah, nice post, but you forgot to address the "Pay to build" element of the game. The shooter side is just one part of the pay to win craze that everyone is hating on. Really I don't think it's fair to builders to give them the new building blocks they wanted and then charge them for it. The main problem is that you have to pay too much for each builder package and there's multiple packages to buy. Builders build, they don't always play the shooter aspect of the game, and now you're forcing them to either be one of the most active players or pay in order to use these new blocks.

The truly sad part is, even with just gameplay these builders cannot afford all the building essentials out there. One package costs 15000 brick points, leaving any builder who hasn't published a map yet 5000 short. Someone who's been around for months may stand a chance of buying these new blocks, but not new guys. And they could easily fix this by just lowering the price of those packages by half at the very least.

title: The Key to Fixing Brick-Force And Other Add-ons

posts.h:
**Read before hating, Different opinions are welcome. I'm trying explain this in a simple way**

1. Merge US and EU Servers.

2. Make rank specific servers.

3. Make Guns have different setbacks and feels.

4. Make the maximum payment of repairing guns 100.

5. Increase the income of force points.

6. Focus on reducing lag and better gameplay.

7. (I know this will probably never be implemented) Make guns have more detail and swag.

8. Make gun holding realistic.

9. Remove warpies and replace with buyable ablities for your character, Such as double jump, leap to side, climb with picks, lie down, and crouch.

10. Make body movement more smooth and realistic.

11. Remove Ammo refills and replace with ammo refill points required before making a map.

12. Make costumes have different setbacks or buffs, ie alien full costume make you double jump, Soldier based costumes can make you climb over walls of 3 blocks high and able to kick and stun enemies.

13. (Buffed version of luck) Make helmets actually have a use in the game. 50% reduced chance of headshot based on how good helmet is.

14. Lower the Force point cost of weapons.

15. Make weapons more affordable for newcomers.

16. Make the maximum cost of a weapon 25,000 force points.

17. Be able to earn bits of armor and newbie clothing by playing games.

18. Lower maximum of armor. Ie 100 armor.

19. Lower the use of gems depending on weapon. ie 5 gems for high damage weapons.

20. Allow to delete weapons

There are many more things to include, but the list is getting to long. Most of these are impossible to do because the mess thats around us, and most of us applied more then 5 gems on weapons. If it was possible but extremely hard to lower the gem usage depending on weapons AND taking away the already applied gems on weapons people own, then do it. For Brick-Force. This game has potential in it, take the chance you have to turn away from the mess that's happening and FIX IT. Just lower the damn cost of the tokens instead of having sales every single week.
CAN WE FIX IT?! YES WE CAN!
posts.t: The Key to Fixing Brick-Force And Other Add-ons
