So, how are we doing today guys? ... Ok. I guess I have to say something. If not, then people will be calling me a troll. Heh. So, here's my say, not yours, though you are free to counter-attack whatever I say or support it. And my previous posts contradict me, I know. It's called trolling. This post of mine will not really have any direction or sequential order. Just me ranting and rambling about random things.

From a real world point of view (always the business side of things), this game will die off if people don't buy these "super items." Infernum is a company, not a charity. People don't do this kind of work without pay, a fact of life. Games are usually made for the entertainment of others with profit as the goal. What would be the profit of making a free game? Seeing these happy emotes "" from reviewers and random people? Yeah, no. The feeling of gratitude would come to you and you would feel all giddy and stuff but honestly? All the hard work you put into that game amounts to practically nothing. Only working for a charity that actually helps people gives you true gratitude. Making a game for the enjoyment of random others? No. The way I worded that sentence makes you think "Well, yeah!", well yeah no. Think about it.

So no money coming from the consumer (us, the wide array of players) = Employees aren't paid, servers receiving no maintenance, the "Boss" receives no profit = Game is effectively shut down for there is no reason to keep it up and running.

For those pro-non-payer people (I think.) Multiple times, constructive feedback that was given to Infernum was that Brick-Force should start to follow a new, more effective version of the "Free to Play" model. In this model, all funding would come from players who bought purely cosmetic clothing which had no game play benefits other than to look cool. This was followed to some extent. During the Halloween and Space updates, a bunch of limited-time clothing popped up in the store, yet they had huge in-game benefits such as armor, XP & FP boosts, etc. though some can argue that they were much like regular clothing that were just max upgraded. So Infernum had listened, just bent the feedback to their benefit. And you think "Greedy pigs" or something along those lines. I say and repeat, a profit-centered company. They played it smart and brought in those items for the consumers who wanted them. They also had clothing that didn't have the upgrades, just in case for the people who wanted to look cool but didn't want to be called a "p2w" or didn't want to be unfair to others. They listened-ish.

Why are people complaining? Balance issues. The "super items" are so rightfully named as these items give the user an advantage over other non-payers as the user gets benefits that non-payers can not easily get in-game without paying and most of time, without "grinding" or putting in hours and hours and hours of work into the game. Still achievable, but really hard. Player progression in this game takes time. And time isn't an easy commodity to get and spend. :/

What irks me are these people who shout out in protest when we come to the issue of "pay 2 win." What is wrong with you? You're mad because some aspects of the game is being paid for. Did you also pay for that new Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 and the console you play it on? -_- What about this computer/technological device that you're looking at right now to read at my random half-@ss ramblings? How much did that cost you? Yet, you're still unwilling to drop $10, €10, C$10, ¥1000 (?), £10 or whatever you use to buy candy and shiz into this game to receive the benefits that you so rightfully hate and dislike yet when you secretly want sooooo badly.

In this game, I can see why people bring up the "p2w" issues so much. It's because the balance issues need an immediate overhaul. However, you blame the payers/"p2w" yet they're the people basically funding the game and in turn keeping the game alive. You blame the people who keep your beloved game alive. How do I know it's beloved to you? YOU FREAKING RAGE. In caps lock. And then they're are the few people who actually give constructive feedback. Instead of getting mad and supporting the death of "p2winners" (extreme I know, but that's how badly their rage is or that's how they exaggerate this issue too much and that is how I perceive it as such) can you please tell your friends and other players to give readable, legible, logical, something constructive feed back about this game to Infernum in some form?

Oh, and before you (the random ignorant reader, no offense if that isn't you) accuse me of being a "p2w" I haven't paid a single cent. Unless you count the laptop and Internet bills that I pay for. Well, not the bills... but you get the point.

HAVE A GREAT DAY Y'ALL.

The issue with the game isn't the F2P model, its systemic balancing problems.
Play in any server and you will see maybe six weapons being used (three basic weapons for free users, three advanced weapons for pay). There are around 25-30 weapons in the game, but only a very select few are being used. The pay users can choose to get the best weapons from the get-go rather than grinding them, giving them an unparalleled advantage.
The problem lies in how the player is rewarded with Force Points, which is given out per kill. The player with the best gun and armor is most likely going to end up with more kills than someone with a lower end gun and no armor. Making it a positive reinforcement loop where the player with the best gear makes more FP, thus being able to buy more stuff to be able to win easier. This causes the rich to become richer and the poor to stay mostly stagnate.
The solution to the P2W problem is to ether revamp the FP acquisition to be more equitable, or to rebalance the weapons to have a sidewise progression rather than a liner one.
All of this has been suggested before, and much of the community aware of it. It's the most debated topic that's ever hit the forums, and the most acknowledgement we've had towards it was a message from a Community Moderator, and I'm pretty sure they don't have much control over balancing with the game if all their reports resulted in no feedback.

Now, as for the balancing, it's actually very simple. Make the weapons far more realistic.

One large problem I have with modern games is that assault rifles are always op. That's not even realistic because it's actually the machine guns that are normally more favourable. So I think of more of a ro-sham-bo approach like so:

Assault and sniper rifles are good against SMGs, shotguns, pistols, and other short-range weapons.
Machine gunners can eat assault and sniper riflemen for lunch.
Close quarter enemies are not good for machine gunners (in reality, LMGs and machine guns in general are actually built for long range uses).

Just like that, every weapon should have its own strength and weakness. That's not among the types of weapons overall, but the weapons within the weapon types. LMGs provide the best examples, like I have mentioned before.

Picking a light machine gun is pretty much rapid fire versus accuracy and mobility versus power. LMGs that do not have much firepower can be lightweight and firing rapidly, while LMGs that do have some firepower may be accurate but would not have as much rapid fire.

title: My ideas on fun, easy to implement (I think) Bricks for Brick Force.

posts.h:
1) High-Powered Springs. When I first was told about the new spring bricks, I imagined shooting into the sky Halo launch pad style, and was really exicted for it. As useful as the new springs are, they were a tiny bit of a letdown for me. So, I think that high-powered springs should be made and put into the function pack. These should look like the normal spring bricks, but instead of being yellow will be a light red. You should be allowed to add 15-20 of these. Basically, they are just like the normal springs, but they send you much-much higher. Especially in very low gravity maps. Yes, I am saying that if you jump on a high-powered spring on -100 gravity, you will go 1.5x higher, or maybe even 2x higher than if you normally jumped. This will put a new twist on aerial combat and could be really cool. However, there's one catch: When going off a high-powered spring, all fall damage is negated. Otherwise, people using the springs would just kinda die, and that wouldn't be much fun :P.

2) Slope springs. These are basically spring bricks mounted on a black slope. Given that slopes already exist, this should be pretty easy to make. They spring you forwards and upwards. I'll use this quick MSPaint doodle to elaborate:

These should also come in normal and high-powered. You should be allowed to add as many normal slope springs as normal springs, and again, 15-20 high-powered slope springs. Why? Well, to be honest, the vertical spring can sometimes kinda suck at clearing gaps. This won't suck as much. This will let people add awesome jumps over cliffs, across buildings, and from spaceship to spaceship in space maps. I'd see many places where I could use one of these.

3)Bullet-proof glass. This is the most simple thing on the list. Basically, make a white-tinted transparent glass brick, and then make it impervious to bullets. I've seen newbies make big areas over the assumption that glass couldn't break, and when I told them otherwise, most of them responded 'ok, that's pretty cool! But why isn't there a type of glass that can't break?'. So I think an unbreakable glass should be implemented. I think about 250 should be allowed, because it shouldn't be that complex, and therefore shouldn't make much lag. This should go in 'deco bricks', and in the sci-fi pack if you REALLY want, but preferably for free.

4) Trapdoor Bricks. Ah, trapdoors. I've seen so many people make maps with traps in them, and I've thought to myself, 'how cool would it be if you could make legitamate traps?'. These bricks would help with that. Basically, they come in 4 different forms: Grass-like trapdoor, Dirt-like trapdoor, Stone-like trapdoor, and Steel-like Trapdoor (These wouldn't be their actual names, but just giving an idea here). They should be pretty hard to tell apart from normal bricks, but they should have a distinguishing color or pattern that pro players can use to tell them apart from regular bricks and avoid them. This would open up many more aspects of gameplay, and correct use of these things could be pretty cool . These would also go into the good ol' function pack, and you could put down about 25 of each type.

5) Teleporters. These would be hard to design and stuff, but these would be sooo cool. Secret areas, map area connections, you name it. There should be 2 green portals (so that you can come in and go out somwhere else, of course), 2 red portals, 2 yellow portals and 2 blue portals. Sure, this makes only 4 complete teleporters, but hey, most maps wouldn't need this many anyhow. A map cannot be registered without a complete portal (basically, if you put 1 portal brick down, the map won't register until you put down the other one), though a map can be registered with no portals, obviously. These would be as big as regular spawn bricks. Again, this is for the increasingly desirable function pack ^^.

6) Conveyor Bricks. An obvious one. You should be allowed to place 50 regular conveyor bricks of each certain direction (North, East, South, and West). The regular conveyors should be traveling at a moderate speed (you can run against it, but you won't be going too fast if you do), and could be very cool. Of course, there should also be (though this is optional) high-speed conveyor bricks, of which 20 can be placed in each direction. This would be impossible to run against, and possibly even impossible to jump against. If you don't like where the conveyor is taking you, the only solution here should be to jump off!

7) Fortified Crates. Basically, these are crates with 2-3 times the amount of health as regular crates. 50 should be allowed to be placed. Great for helping fortify an in-game stronghold. This can go in the function pack, though this should really come free.
posts.t: My ideas on fun, easy to implement (I think) Bricks for Brick Force.
posts.e: Last edited by quicklite; 04.01.2013 at 18:04. Reason: typos schmypos

posts.h:
Continued!

8) Loose Dirt. This has half the life of regular crates. About 100-150 of these should be allowed. Nice for secret tunnels and stuff which you'd want players to uncover without wasting too much ammo.

9) Powered Ladders. Ladders which move like treadmills, and which can be climbed up REALLY fast. Only 100 of these should be allowed. Ever had a huge climb in your map where you think to yourself 'There's gotta be a quicker way to have people do this'? Well, this would be the solution.

10) Overcharged Beacons.. These are Beacons that instead of just doing that siren thing, just give off a TON of light. Only 15 of these should be allowed. It should look like a Beacon, just a little bit more futuristic, and with white light instead of yellow light. It would go great with maps that have a 'core'. As in like a core of a ship, or just a place that's supposed to be really hot, or something. Would be nice. This would go into the Sci-Fi pack.

11) Water Bricks. Simple enough. Blocky water bricks. there shouldn't be any water physics to this (that would be too hard), but it should still act like water, as in you can sink and swim through it, a little like minecraft water. Heck, you could even add an oxygen limit that you can stay underwater, and then add a scuba mask that negates said limit. Plus, water negates fall damage. Yes, I know that if you fall from high up enough water doesn't really negate fall damage irl anymore, but hey, why bother being realistic? It's a game! I couldn't see this being too hard to program, and it sure would be better than the 'light blue brick water' that you get in many maps, mine included ^^. You should be allowed to place 250-300 of these, because for pools of water, you need a lot of water :P.

12) Priority Spawn Unlocker. These are spawn areas that you have to capture yourself. These go for all game-modes. In team game-modes, you capture this block for your team. In free-for-all, you capture this for yourself. Basically, these are spawns which you capture with the E button (just like defusion) to make them your own. Now, you won't always spawn here, but it will be an extra spawn point, and an inevitable advantage against the other team, especially if the spawn point is located in a cool position. You should be allowed to place 3 of these, as 3 is a good number ^^.
This brick was suggested by Blauze

13) The ability to build 10 bricks beneath the original ground in 1F maps. Yes, this isn't a Brick, but this is still vital. I've always wondered why this isn't possible. I mean, why not? In 100x100 maps, I've always wanted to fly below the map with a jetpack and build a tunnel that way. Hand-making a 5F 100x100 map is a complete pain and takes up precious loading time in bricks. 50x50 5F maps are 50x50 maps, and I usually prefer to work with more space. A pre-made 5F 100x100 map, as I said earlier, would cause way too much lag from all the excess bricks. The solution is pretty simple: Just move that original ground bit 10 bricks above that invisible barrier. I mean, this won't jeopardize the height at all: I've played this map called 'Vertigo', which is this beautiful, awe-inspiring tower that goes to the vertical limit (which is just HUGE) but is actually impossible to find anyone and fight in :P. That height -10 bricks won't change anything. And that will let jetpack users fly underneath their map and put in a few tunnels and whatnot where necessary. Why not?

14) Make a darker Skybox. At the moment, even the nighttime skyboxes seem to make everything lit up. For dark/stealth based maps, it would be great if there could be a skybox which isn't like daytime, where you could hide in shadows, avoid lit up areas (for stealth purposes) and be in places where it is literally to dark to see. I don't think this would be too hard to do.
This idea was suggested by FPEngineer

15) Add a wider variety of color bricks. It would be nice to have an entire pallet of color bricks to use and experiment with. This wouldn't cause much extra lag, would be incredibly easy to implement, and would be really nice to have. Why not?
This idea was suggested by FPEngineer.

Man, I hope Lenus or someone sees this. As tricky as some of these might be, this game would do great with some. If you have an idea, post it below! If it's good, I'll put it on the list.

16) Add more variety in the turrets. The turrets are great, but they are pretty similar. What would be nice is if a few different kinds of turrets were made. How cool would it be to have a turret that fires rockets? What about arcing grenades, like the Shark? What about a turret that does less damage than the cannon, but is very long-range? What about an auto-shotgun turret is great for crowd control, but overheats quickly? The only problem I could see with this is that it would over-lag the game, but you could always make it so that you could put 1 turret each. After all, that would mean that builders would be encouraged to use all the different kinds!
This idea was suggested by FPEngineer and modified by quicklite

17) Doors. Ah, doors. The one thing that Brick Force lacks. There should be several kinds: Single Doors, Double Doors, Wooden Doors, Space Doors, Iron Doors, the likes. You should be allowed to open and close them with the e button. Also, it would be a good idea to put a door in the tutorial so that newbies don't get stuck trying to open them. This will allow you to be more stealthy (close it behind you now), and make maps, especially urban maps, more realistic.
This idea was suggested by FPEngineer

18) More fire. This one's simple. More variety in fire! Perhaps blue flames that kill you twice as fast? Big, 4x4 fires for cool fire pits? Hey, maybe you could even include a trap that shoots fire at unsuspecting brick-men! This would be great for trap maps.
This idea was suggested by FPEngineer. Thanks for all the help, man!

19) Path bricks. A twist on elevators. Make 20-30 bricks which will follow a 1x1 path back and forth, a little like the bees in defense much, just, well, back and forth. This will not only allow people to make elevators, but it will let people make moving platforms, complex obstacles, and just add another twist to the game. You should be allowed to put down 200 of the moving brick path bricks. These are shared between all the elevator bricks.
This idea was suggested by FPEngineer and tbh is my favourite idea of his ^^

----------Useless Part-----------
Those are some great ideas ;) Especially the slope springs (I still wonder why they didn't think of making this block for brickstar) and the teleporters, which are something I was going to suggest too. However I'm not a big fan of the overcharged beacons, but that might be because I'm not sure about what you mean by "TON of light", I don't want to be blinded by a block like I'd be with a flashbang... Although it could be fun^^

I don't have any ideas right now since I just woke up, but since you're accepting any idea as long as it's good, I should probably suggest the best block from my own topic, the PSU. If I remember correctly, I didn't receive any negative feedback for this one, so here you go.

Originally Posted by Blauze
Priority Spawn Unlocker.

Basically it's a checkpoint-style, flagpole-shaped block. when a team captures it by touching the block, a blue or red flag is raised depending on which team controls it, and it unlocks 2 (or 4, depending on the block's version) new spawns around the flag which have a higher priority than the basic spawns. Meaning you'll be more likely to spawn at the new location. Imagine a "king of the hill" map : This block would be atop of the hill, and give the ability to control the area to the best team. It could also work as checkpoints for longer parkour / jump and run maps. If one team controls the PSU, the other team can reclaim it if they manage to touch it themselves.

title: Petition to put the Browser Version of Brick-Force on Kongregate.

posts.h:
Those of you who have never heard of Kongregate may be wondering: Why the heck should we do this? What is it about Kongregate that is special enough to need a petition asking it to be there? The reason is simple: Kongregate has literally millions of visitors every day. And it supports unity games. And it has done this exact thing for inspiring unity (or java) multiplayer game developers, helping them massively boost the size of their community. I could name several if necessary. "But why do we need people?", you may ask. "Isn't the EU community big enough?". Yes, but we could all agree that the US community sure as heck is not. And kongregate is mostly US! And since Infernum is a big(-ish) company, all it needs to do is strike up a deal with Kongregate, and it'll put the browser edition of Brick Force right up on the front page with a few badges (kongregate-based achievements) to lure people in (Kongregate will do that, no need for Infernum to worry). Heck, it even has a 'Kreds' system, which is basically Kongregate's currency that can be bought with real money and converted back into real money, which will work great for Brick Force. You can have a Kreds to Tokens option ^^.

How this would work: When people enter the browser version of Brick Force on kongregate, they should be allowed to use their kongregate accounts, which if done in collaboration with kongregate, shouldn't be that hard to do. If the person is new, a little window pops up and says 'choose your username', and once they have done that, they go to the tutorial and so on. Kongregate also have a little forum place which will exist for kongregate's brick force, but there should be some sort of link to the official forums as well. There should also be something that allows you to download Brick-Force off kongregate, as the browser version doesn't work so well with a few people, and that will help more kong users successfully enjoy brick force, and will provide a quick solution to inevitable kong users wanting a more fluid option than the Browser version (I'm not saying that the browser version isn't adequate, because it is, I'm just saying that some people might find the downloadable more useful ^^)

Who knows, maybe people will like it. After all, if it hits big enough after its time up on the front page, it'll get a permanent position there in the 'Multiplayer Games' tab of the front page, attracting yet more people. If done right, it could give the US server the revive of people it badly needs.

So, what do you guys think? If you support this, let me know, and I'll add your name to the petition. If I get enough people, I'll add it to the 'Open Discussion Feedback Thread'. Because it will look more impressive that way ^^

title: Automatically change the ammo refill item based on equipped weapon

posts.h:
So now there's a rudimentary interface for switching weapons, which is a good thing. There is one problem with it, though: ammo refills.

If I go into a match with a light weapon and light ammo refill equipped, and then notice it's a sniper map, I can switch to a sniper rifle without too much trouble, great. However, I then cannot refill my ammo because I still have the light refill on my action bar. Not so great.

My idea would be to automatically change these refill items based on the weapon equipped and the round type.

For example, if I switch to a sniper rifle, it should automatically move the sniper refill into my action bar. If I join a pistol-only round, automatically switch to secondary refill.

Another idea would be to remove all the heavy/medium/light/long refill items and make a new "main weapon refill" item that just works for all main weapons regardless of type. There's really no reason to have all these different items at all.

So, over the months, people might have seen the little bits of feedback I've been giving for Brick Force in my various threads. Now, I've decided to collect all the feedback I've given about Build Mode onto one single thread for neatness and for reference. The blue ideas are links, and idea 6) is just a compliation of all pieces of build mode advice from threads not worth linking to. Read all the bits, and tell me what you think. I might add more bits in the future, though that is only if I feel like something needs to be added. Which idea do you think is the most worthy of implementation?

1) My New Brick Ideas.

2) My idea on moving maps across servers.

3) My idea on testing maps.

4) My idea on improving explosive/toxic barrels.

5) My idea on Group Maps.

If you wanna build ur map with someone else, you send a 'map invitation' to them. This works exactly like a clan invitation, but if you accept, their map pops up in a 'shared maps' toolbar, and you gain leader priviliges to the map, meaning that whatever you do is saved to their map, just like whatever they do is. This shared maps toolbar is 5 maps big (10 for premium) and you can take maps off this-list cost free (no tokens OR Force/Brick Points). This would allow people to truly co-operate on maps ^^. I know this can be abused which is why you've gotta trust the guy you're sending it to and established building plans and whatnot. I could see many people who I'd do this with .

6) Other miscellaneous ideas.

- Allow map-builders to earn 1 Brick Point for every 30 bricks placed on someone else's map. It would encourage people to co-operate on each others maps by adding an 'incentive' of sorts, and it would also mean that when you come to publish your own map, you have more experience off helping others.

-Make 'Brick count' a viable map factor in the Brick HQ. It'll be interesting! :P

- Add an upgrade or something onto the jetpack that gives it a function which you can turn off and on that makes you move (vertically and horizontally) 3 times as fast. Nice for getting around larger maps.

All your ideas are wonderful and should be considered heavily. Especially 2, 3, and 4. Being able to port maps across servers would be a splendid feature. A more easier way of testing maps would also really help builders with their building experience. And lets face it, explosive and toxic barrels really need improvement. As of now, they're rather useless. They aren't really that deadly, even when put them at key points. In the time you could take to shoot the barrel, you could have just killed the player instead sadly.

1, The brick ideas also has great suggestions. However I'm a bit worried if adding too many interactive blocks could make brick-force harder to run for some computers. And they would need a lot of work to implement this features into the game fluidly. Interactive blocks seem like they'd be a lot of work.

And well, I do have a grip about 5 actually. As you've said, you know it could be abused, and the only problem I have against it is people don't always understand features of Brick-force to their fullest. A lot of people might not realise that other people can abuse this and destroy all their hard work or something like that. We might get some drama about people deleting each other's maps. It might actually hurt some players' experience as opposed to helping it. It would be nice if Infernum could add some group map feature, but I think they'd need some good countermeasures ready in place before doing so.

And finally 6. This idea is fantastic. We need a way to pump brick points into the system, without just giving them away. And this would work, even if they don't follow your suggestion to the letter. It's really the idea and what it solves that counts. Most players can't afford to build with brick-points. Any released maps will most likely not earn you back the points you spent making the map.

Thanks for the feedback, DrRaven! I know what you mean about idea 1. That idea isn't supposed to have all of its ideas implemented. It's just a massive list of possible cool bricks :3. Though ideas 1 and 2 on the Idea 1 list (hope that made sense ^^) should be easy enough to do. I mean, they've already got the mechanism, a few other versions couldn't hurt.

title: Typewriter - Wiki Revival! Ideas for the Wiki's Future

posts.h:
From what we all notice is that the Brick-Force wiki is presumed dead by observers, well, it is alive, barely. But this idea is the Wiki's defibrillator! Most people just contribute to the Wiki just for the community title, some say me but I have a valid reason - The Forums - I am mostly active here and since I'm focused in school I don't play much and I just type and help people while two or three books are only my lap. But we are here for a legitimate reason. And it is to revive the wiki with ideas that will inspire players to actively contribute and keep the wiki's heart pumping in a moderate pace! I call it - Project:Typewriter - Let's start, shall we?

Interest
When editing a wiki page, editors will usually read what is written before editing it and adding or removing something if it is already written, this way the editors will know much more of the item and might spark an interest into the reader and view every page and read and edit! (read rewards) If a player have earned a reward such as the Typewriter 101, players in-game will begin to question "Where did he get that weapon?", then he/she will begin to scour the Wiki and find it and learn that it is earned through contributing, therefore with a high chance he/she will be interested in contributing! And repeat the circle of interest.

Rewards
Every contribution to the Wiki seems useless for most players. Since the item's statistics are just displayed in the weapon mouse-over layout. But here is a buzzer! Every contribution can earn the player some rewards, weapons, equipments, actions and more! The rewards will inspire every player to contribute, read, learn and have fun in-game!
More contributions, more rewards, more editors, more readers and more health points for the wiki! Every contribution counts, if the player have reached over 101 helpful contributions, he/she will earn the Typewriter 101!

Effects
(read interest) Many players will probably begin contributing because of the circle of interest, which means more work and more wiki account checking, so yeah. Y'know what will happen. BOOM! Sudden burst of wiki page edits. BAM! Lots of players have contributed 101 information.

You - the reader - can help me in Project:Typewriter and revive the wiki by supporting this idea!

Dear Brick-Force,

A few days ago, I heard that Unity3D would soon support consoles such as the Nintendo Wii U, Microsoft Xbox 360, and Sony Playstation 3. I was wondering, since Brick-Force uses the Unity3D engine, why not make Brick-Force on other consoles? This would help lure more players in.

Suggestions

I would obviously suggest a new control scheme. For example, on the Wii U, the control scheme could be:

Brick-Force Play Mode

Left Analog Stick - Move right, left, front and back.
Right Analog Stick - Look right, left, front, back, up, and down.
Control Pad Right and Left/L and R Buttons - Scroll through weapons.
Control Pad Up and Down - Reload
B Button/ZL Button - Jump
A Button/ZR Button - Shoot
Y Button - Chat
X Button - Action Panel Uses
+ Button - Pause Menu
- Button/Touch Screen - Select or for miscellaneous uses.

Brick-Force Build Mode

Left Analog Stick - Move right, left, front and back.
Right Analog Stick - Look right, left, front, back, up, and down.
B Button/ZL Button - Jump
Y Button - Chat
+ Button - Pause Menu
- Button/Touch Screen - Select or for miscellaneous uses.
Control Pad Right and Left/L and R Buttons - Scroll through tools.
B Button Pressed Two Times - Jetpack enabled.
X Button - Select brick.
A Button - Shoot brick.

I really hope you approve this.

Kind regards, Manguy

This is my idea. So don't hesitate to give me some feedback. Also this is my first thread. So, here we go.

Balancing Sniper Rifles. Add bullet drop. for example, in Battlefield play4free, Sniper rifles have bullet drop to balance out the game. Is was thinking "Headshot, Headshot, another headshot... man this is way too easy. hey should balance this." So, I was thinking, why not make it a bit more realistic? So, I played a few rounds of Battlefield and thought of bullet drop. This way, sniper rifles won't be so OP like everyone calls them. You'll have to aim higher than the head so you can get a headshot. Even the less-skilled players can use a sniper rifle with ease. this also adds a challenge. I also thought that regular weapons could use bullet drop too as weapons with high damage are most of the time really accurate. as I said earlier, this adds a bit of realism and challenge to the game. the more skillful players will also have to learn this. If a player say goes to the left, you will have to predict the velocity and BPS ( Bricks Per Second) of your gun. For example if I was running and a sniper about 100 bricks away from would plan to get a head shot said sniper will have to aim above the head and to the direction said player was running.

sure, it is easy to make brick-shots, but i don't think snipers are this OP anymore.
They WERE in the closed beta last year, but they aren't anymore, just as i think.
Just look around and you'll see many guys walking around using their fully upgraded 5-stars-weapon with at least 200 lives.
idk what is more powerful. A bad Sniper or a bad "normal" player...but anyway, i think the bad "normal" player just has more chances to hit the sniper. those were my experiences.

so if you'd like to balance them, i'd say you should make them a bit stronger. but anyway, then they would really be too strong, so...just let them how they are now.
I agree but once on a map I was sniping people really easily and got a score of like 34/0/3

Mmm... random fact of the day: We use paintballs, not bullets! So... paint drop? Mmm... watching paint dry is not fun. Especially on a windy day in Fall when all these leaves stick to the wall you're painting on and... don't paint in Fall. You'll regret it.

Righto, back on topic...

Quick three part question: If you remember, which map were you playing on, what sniper riffle were you using, and what kind of players were you up against?

Anyways, we can still apply bullet drop to our paintball using weapons. Yes, bullet drop can affect how players shoot and play. But it won't make that much of a difference as many maps are small and the bullet drop will decrease as the map size does. Then again, we'll have vice-versa as the maps will increase in size. However, many maps force the player into close tactical situations where bullet drop won't do much, unless you have a high recoil weapon and your bullets just spray all over the enemy. It's an interesting concept if we apply all these random other variations and all these other thingys.

Bullet drop has a flat learning curve though. Once you know where the bullet will hit, it's just like not having bullet drop. Many players will pick that skill up in a couple of matches.

So yeah. +1 to your bullet drop feedback. Well, to me it's more like +0.9 to this idea. But that's still "good."

Here's a way to balance snipers, take out the Boa, Cobra, and every sniper better than those.

But in all seriousness, although this may relieve sniper victims from long-distance fire, there's also the question of quick-scoping snipers, who probably wouldn't be affected at that distance (and who I personally think are a bigger problem than long-distance snipers). Aiming down the scope should be much slower than the instant-aim the game currently has, and the character should lose accuracy while moving and aiming.

These are a few of my ideas for new function bricks. Don't worry, the list won't be overwhelming. I also want advice on how to improve them or simplify them. Well, not much more to say here. Here's the list:

1. Cannon
--Cannons will take up the same space and function similarly to turrets, but will have some differences. Cannons will fire powerful 75-damage, armor-piercing rounds, but will instantly have to cool down for about 4 seconds. You should probably know what it should look like (Note: Armor-piercing means that armor will still have an effect on the damage, but will have less influence than normal) Max. 2

2. Cushion Brick
--These fancy bricks let players who land on them ignore fall damage completely. This would be helpful for players who want a quick route down for their maps, or who want players to survive if they fall on a certain area. They come in 3 colors (Blue, red, and green), each exactly like the color-bricks of the same color, except that the cushion bricks don't glow. There should be a max. of 8 bricks of each color, allowing for 6 2x2 cushion platforms

3. Sticky Brick
--Only one word to describe this brick--annoying. These bricks slow player movement and decrease jumping height by 50%. Remember that attack speed is still unaffected, and grenades still bounce off like normal. The brick has a medium-dark brown color and a smooth wave pattern on each side. Max. 45

4. Vines
--They're just vines, what can they do, right? The two flat, tendril-like vines with a DNA-like patterns are climbable. This could be an alternative to ladders for nature-based maps, serve as decoration, or could be like a secret entrance when set against the right block ...They will be identical to ladders in every manner except appearance. Unlimited.

5. Spikes
--This is a very basic idea. Steel spikes damage players adjacent to them or on top of them at the rate as fires. But unlike fires, they are solid. They look about 3/4 of a normal block's size, but when stood on are actually only 1/2 a normal block's height (Not that sanding on it's a good idea). Max. 25

6. Fireworks
--It sounds crazy, but you'll understand in a minute. There are explosive barrels, but these work differently. When shot at, they fire straight up to a height of about 6 or 7 blocks, (Or until intercepted by a brick or player) and explodes. It deals heavy damage to anything caught inside the blast, and can also be used as a signal flare (Though it can be seen by the other team). Max. 5

7. Smokebox
--*Cough* *Cough*, Where is this smoke coming from?? The Smokebox is where. These are medium-light wooden crates are filled with black coals and powders that cause smoke to rise out from the box. The top is open, allowing smoke to rise up like a small Smokie explosion. The smoke does rise through blocks, in a pillar about 4 blocks tall and 3 bricks wide. These could simply be decorative items, making maps more realistic, or could be used to strategically block players' vision in certain areas. Max. 10

8. Slippery Brick
--Warpies don't work so well now, do they? The Slippery Brick makes players on top of them slip as the try to move around, continuing in the direction they moved in. Players who attempt to change direction will find it harder, but the sliding does slow over time (The faster the initial speed, the longer you slide). They come in 3 colors (Blue, sky blue, and light grey), each exactly like the color bricks of the same color, except for 2 differences: They don't glow, and the tops are slightly lighter than the rest of the brick. Max. 10

9. Trap Door
--Simple idea, really. When a player steps on a trap door brick, it will "open" causing players on that space to wall through for about 2.5 seconds. It will then close again, ready for the next victim. It looks like a wooden brick with a line on the top and bottom. This could be a trap, or a good entryway when paired with Cushion Bricks. Max. 10

10. Oil
--You don't want to be near a fire with this stuff. It is a flat brick that resembles a dark splotch on the ground that connects with other oil near it. While standing in this stuff, you take twice the damage from fires. Other than that, it's just decoration. Max. 50

title: A way to play Build Mode: Offline!

posts.h:
Hello! I have a presentation for all of you!

I was thinking that people should be able to build maps off-line, with their accounts. Keeping themselves "off-line"
so they can't be seen by anyone. And also not directly connected to the server, so they won't lag due to Internet connections.

People who build maps has this issue: The bricks spawn or get deleted very slowly no matter what Brick-Gun is used to build.

An off-line mode would help a lot of players. This way, no one would lag while building or get disconnected.

But of course, you need to log-in first, in order to retrieve profile data.



As with the image I've provided: Using the "settings" option in the Launcher, players who select to start in offline mode will able to well... Play Build Mode offline! But like I said, you need to Log-in once to retrieve data, and you'll need a Internet connection to save.

It'll be faster, and your connection won't be chained to everyone else's, nor the entire serverbase.

This way: You'll build faster, smoother, more privately... And no one will ever know.

What do you think?

This post contains my biased opinion meant for the purpose of debates or discussions of constructive feedback.

I am purposely posting this here. For all eyes. Please do not see this as a post full of hate.

For like I said, this is a rant.
Criticism coined in a harsh way. Since from what I seen, being a nice guy ain't gonna fix anything.

I repeat: This isn't mean to be offensive, or a "verbal attack" on anything.
I love this game, but there are many things that I should point out.

Issue on of the unbalancement of Brick-Force.

5-Stars can be Over Powered, it's because of the Upgrades is why their OP.

If not, you could easily take down a guy with a Spider, Hornet, Drake, Orion or whatever 5-Star you think is tough... With a Black Widow. There's also the armor issue as well. You can't fight a juggernaut with 140 armor if your a newbie!

I have already stated this, even sneaking behind the back to take the guy with armor out is futile.

Before you can even take half of his health away, he'll just snap back to you-- and pulverize you in a second. To top it off, the person might use a 100 HP potion on the spot to give him even more health. Doesn't matter if your a sneaking James Bond, or an Assassin.

Now... 100 HP (Health Points) +140 AP (Armor Points) +100 Health Regen = a whopping 340 HP.

It doesn't matter which tactic you use, unless you attack that juggernaut with all your friends with all the ammo you got... I can say most people doesn't have a chance.

But why on earth nerf the snipers? In Real-Life or in games, if shot to the head or the brain--they are supposed to kill.
Of all the feedback we gave, this is their bright idea?

By all things, the radius on Grenades should be nerfed. I hate to bring up the nade-spam issue myself, I feel as if I'm complaining constantly.

I could assure that, if we didn't have the upgrade system this wouldn't even be discussed.

However, currently the idea of removing the upgrade system is a thing that shouldn't be suggested. In a different way, there should be a way around it without removing or replacing the current system.

I know what some others are gonna say... "But then how are they gonna make money smartass?"
Yeah, a company who gave out iPhones and iPad's as prizes shouldn't be thought of a "poor" company.

A company who can get stuff like that, can produce. They can make merchandise for the games they have.
Now some others may also say: "What could they make? T-Shirts? Figures? Posters... etc? I wouldn't buy that."
Well some wouldn't, some would.

But right now, I don't think many would. Brick-Force needs to grow, but I'll get to that, moving along.

We kinda suggested the idea of Disabling Upgrades for Weapons and Armor separately as a room option. It'll just disable the upgrades, nothing else and you could turn it off and on.

Some think that no one would buy tokens afterwards... I ask: Should tokens only work for upgrades? Nope.

Although as an Agent I keep Ideas like this confidential, I don't think there's a point in hiding it since other players have come up with the same idea, or at least thought this was a good idea.

I have yet to meet one soul who disagrees with this idea, and tells me why. It's also the easy way!

Of all things that are thought of. This idea, should be implemented. Or else Brick-Force ain't never going to grow.

Look around guys. Is there anyone making Brick-Force videos? Maybe 4-5 channels are, but what can they feature about Brick-Force? The unfair issues? I only know Schilling--a German Youtuber who makes videos, and I guess that's why Brick-Force has a lot of German players, aside from it being developed by a German company.

Lets imagine a Youtuber you watch makes a video on Brick-Force. Do you think he or she will be praising the game?
Or let's say websites like MMOhut.

That answer, is no. They'll be barely playing the game due to unfair issues. Then throw the game away calling it "crap".

Most of this Youtuber's followers will think the same like him, and shame the game calling it "crap" as well.
Some maybe cheery when they play with the people they know, but when they decide to play with others, they'll meet the players with the heavy advantage.

If this issue ain't fixed the way we like it... I wouldn't say "kiss Brick-Force goodbye" but, I'd say "keep struggling while other companies Free-to-play games turn into a cashcow".
posts.t: Issue on of the unbalancement of Brick-Force. (Pay-to-win issue)

posts.h:
Brick-Force and artistic-contributing players.

It's OK for the company to screw up sometimes. But last time I checked, this is the third time in the row!

The upgrade system was OK at the start. But issues went on and on, but were completely ignored.
If anyone can prove me wrong, go on: Explain. If it wasn't, we wouldn't be talking about it Pay-to-win stuff now would we? Even if it wasn't, how should we know? Any posts, or guts to talk about this on a Facebook post?

Secondly: Many contests went haywire. Most of you don't know of course, there was an Outfit contest, a weapon and an old map contest.

In the Closed Beta Map contest, the winner was the map "Terminal", a replica from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2's map. Although I say kudos to the builder Vorvk, but the Facebook COD fanboy's gave his design so many likes that he automatically won.

The weapon contest went beserk due to a "Watergun entry" that didn't even had any work on it's design:

But the person who made it got his friends outside of Brick-Force to vote for his entry via likes, while designs of mine the "BAR-97", Sinyx's "Melee Phone" and the winner Matiazo's "Bee Shotgun" were almost forgetten.

We have pleaded that the idea of adding the watergun should be reconsidered, but disagreed.

Thankfully Matiazo's weapon was the album cover, and he got some support from the forums.

Other wise we'd have a Watergun. Not a Force-Point shotgun. Maybe shotgun's would never be added.

LINK: http://www.brick-force.com/forum/sho...contest+design

Now here comes the "Outfit design contest"!
Gravebear's "Panda outfit" was a very unique idea in fact! But it killed all the other players hard worked entries because many thought it was "cute", and neglected the other entires.

As the community we advised the idea of having the Top 3 outfits in the game since it's not hard adding outfits rather than weapons... but this idea was entirely declined.

LINK: http://www.brick-force.com/forum/sho...contest+design

All of this will cause, and already has, the artistic and contributing players to leave the game.

Have I already mentioned most of them had? Is Lochie making videos?
DrDrisko ain't coming back. What happened to HojjoshMC?

They left the game. Brick-Force ain't a place for casual gaming artists anymore.

Also, was it the Most played map contest?..

Now for this part, I'm gonna say what I saw. There was this other contest issue where who's map gets most played will get an iPad or something.
Usually, "Kerian2", yes the guy who made freaking epic "Keriancity" was going to get it.

But then, it seemed that the builder who made a "Spongebob" map got more played, and the winner was changed.
Well ain't that nice?

Kerian: -"Yay, I won!"
-"Well, woops! Screw you, we made a mistake and we'll give it to a guy who made a total copy of a famous TV show!"
(Maybe I'm harsh there, but unless you contacted Kerian, I don't think I'm doing a mistake.)

Speaking of Kerian, where did he go? Or did he get mad at this (Wouldn't blame him) and leave?
Applause! There goes another splendid artist!

Lack of Communication with the Brick-Force community.

I know Dragon Prophet is important, but thats enough! The Brick-Force community is being neglected with all the issues intact.

The Facebook, Twitter and Tumblr pages of Brick-Force isn't that active as it was in Beta or after beta was done.

You barely share anything about Brick-Force, or bricks, even when we gave you ideas.
posts.t: Lack of Communication with the Brick-Force community.

posts.h:
Rant on the uselessness of Brick-by-Brick.

Thing is, it always says "come here more for some brick-force tactics" in the end.

Can anyone mention one tactic, aside from the Golden Thunder 18K commercial and other 5-Star weapon commercials?

That's all I see of these series. Commercials.

Not even one video can help a newcomer there. You are only showing 5-Star equipment that more than 60% of the players cannot or don't purchase.

Look at the infographics:

http://25.media.tumblr.com/tumblr_m8...fyqo1_1280.jpg

http://cdn.infernum.com/WebAssets_20...013-03-012.png

Do you see majority of anyone using 5-Stars?

NOTE:

BP40- Black Widow

BR4--Hurricane

BWM-- Boa

BSG69-- Cobra

BK47- Thunder

None of these are 5-Stars. I know these are old info graphics. But still, join a match and you'll see many of the players with these weapons. Not 5-Stars.

Why not feature these weapons? Shouldn't weapons that are used a lot be featured?

Or are you telling us that these weapons actually suck, and can't find a good thing to show about these weapons?

Also, if anyone's is going to say: "Hey, they have videos about Build mode tips!"

Those aren't even tips! That's just "Build mode for dummies!". Who doesn't even know how to use a Brick-Gun? (No offense by the way. But it's not that hard to register a map. People know how to register maps without this video.)

Some people wants to make a good map sometimes. But they don't even know a clue how.
Why not mention some tips from us? I thought there were gonna be some tips from us.

People want to Build a "Sarios"! A "Matrixius"! A "Dusty"! A "Colony"! A "Corefusion"! And they want to know how!

...But hell, lets just show people how to use a swappie.

Seems legit... (Sarcasm)

Not to mention nobody even cares about the map spotlight videos.

Also, about the Weapon Class review videos. Such as the "Assault Rifle", "Grenades" and so on...

Again: You are only showing commercials of those weapons. Not how to handle them.

People want to learn how to use those weapons! Not know what they are.


"This gun does 30 Damage!"





We can see that on the info on the gun... but Damage ain't only important--recoil and Rate-of-fire (ROF) is as important!

I hope I'm able to explain. This series is barely helpful to anyone.

Can anyone say that these series actually helped you? And how?

If anyone says "It helped me with this".

Out of 25+ videos-- this is all it helped you with?

My idea is: Show stuff that'll actually help the players.

At least mention the guides we all made...

I've heard that they were going to mention or make a video that includes some tips we gave out...
...but then again. I don't think so anymore.

The series is just for ametures. Maybe before the "Ametures" level. Not for intermediate players who seek to get better in game.

I'm sorry for sounding negative. --But my engine doesn't only run on optimism. It also runs on realism.

Now I'm sorry to poke my nose here.

But I want to say this: Some of the Chosen MoTW aren't even being played...
OK, sometimes they are... but I can only see about 2 Rooms with a MoTW map on the EU. I went and saw the EU server, I saw results that I didn't expect. ( I visited via Browser version)

Of course, at the time I came--It could have been a time, where no one was playing the MoTW map.

Oh, but don't make me say anything the US. Barely anyone gives a crap about MoTW there.

Guys, I don't think even if we pick any user, no ones going to give a damn.
So it doesn't even matter if he or she already has the "Brainy Builder" title or not.

A long time ago, everyone would discuss and say:

A-"Woah, you know that map?"
B-"That map? Pffft, that one sucks, the other one was better."
C-"I think both of them were good, I liked what he made there!"
I mean, many people used to give a DAMN about MoTW. They cared!
There's also this, lets say my map became MoTW. So?

Normally, it's awesome! But: Only when people goes and says: "Wow, good job man!"

If no one plays this persons MoTW map, then whats the point of it?

Also, whenever there was a MoTW, there was a Forum discussion about it.

I want to you guys to look at this:

http://www.brick-force.com/en/news/m...by-anixian-944

http://www.brick-force.com/forum/sho...ius-by-Anixian

When you look at them, you'll see in the website post, that this was said:

We hope you all enjoy this map as much as we do, and be sure to give Anixian a shout over on our forums.


There's was a Forum page about the map, not only mine, but others too!
I was so happy when I got all that feedback, as a builder! Why doesn't anyone do this anymore?

Also, everyone-- please go check the Brick-Force Facebook page here, and read the comments of the MoTW maps posted there.

http://www.facebook.com/BrickForce

See?

You'll see that no one even talks about the map. No one cares about it. Possibly only 3~4 of 30 comments talk about the map.

I'm making a map soon. Racoura has awesome maps, so does GraveBear, SiNNiR, clone117, Saimen, and so on!
BUT. It doesn't matter what they make, what they'll make will go to waste.

Because, the MoTW business isn't taken seriously. Both by officials and community.

Like I just said: Even if you get a MoTW, other than your mom-- no one cares.

In this thread I'll be introducing several new types of Boomers. I tried to make each one as unique as possible, and I did include pictures of each one. (They're not that great, but I did my best) If you have any questions, post them below. Well, there's not much more to say here, so let's get started, shall we?


The BOOM-erang

-"A new style of weapon which is designed to fly straight at your opponents. They'll think it's just a toy until it detonates!"

Yes, you saw it right. My first idea is a boomerang- well, sort of. When you throw the BOOM-erang, It'll fly in an (almost) straight line in whatever direction you're facing. It detonates upon contact with any sort of brick, making it a good explosive for far-off opponents. But this thing is shaped like a boomerang- if it doesn't intercept anything before it travels 50 bricks, it'll curve around and come right back to where it was thrown (At this point, It's a good idea to change location). But if you're smart, this curve can be used to hit your enemies from behind. Keep in mind that the BOOM-erang isn't lightning fast- your opponents will have time to react before it explodes. (At least you get 2 of them)

Tiny Ticker

-"Be sure to run like crazy after you plant it."

The second item on my list is the Tiny Ticker (Cheesy name, right?). As you may have assumed, I have created a mini time bomb. You plant it just as you would a Boomslang, only this time, you have 7 seconds until it explodes. "But Dax... The Boomslang lasts a lot more than 7 seconds, and it hurts anyone who runs across it! Why would we need this?" I'll explain that now. The Tiny Ticker is about as small as the Boomslang, but doesn't have the blue line, making it less noticeable. (Instead, you'll hear a quiet ticking sound which gets faster as the bomb gets closer to detonating) Also, the Ticker doesn't require anyone to run within a tiny area to function. It'll take some practice and luck, but you can figure out how to master this Boomer. (But even if you fail at first, you get a second one)

The Mecha-Bomb
-"This complicated ball of electronics is the only existing grenade that electrocutes those who are affected by it."

Electricity is a complicated thing, isn't it? The Mecha-Bomb shocks anyone caught in it's blast, paralyzing them for a few moments. This means that movement is impossible and moving the crosshair is substantially slower than usual (Along with the irritating twitching). Melee weapons won't be able to be used during this time, but weapon switching is possible (But slower). Everyone else gets an advantage over those affected, but remember that guns can still shoot during paralysis. You get 2 of these.

Relic Boomer
-This is believed to be a weapon used by ancient civilizations. We're not sure if it's magic or just a fancy smoke machine."

How to describe this... Well, put simply, it's just like the Snowball Menace, except that it detonates like a normal grenade (A few seconds after you pop off the cap). When thrown, this ancient weapon leaves behind a trail of green smoke. After it explodes, it creates a cloud of this dark smoke, where anyone inside of it takes damage over time (Just like the Snowball Menace, and at the same damage rate too). This weapon does bounce around like your average Boomer instead of detonating upon impact. Is there really much more I can add to this?

Well, that's all I've got for now. I might add some more Boomers later on.

title: LEGACY items and level restricted use not buy

posts.h:
I think, instead of making it so that you have to be a certain level in order to buy a weapon, it should be a certain level to equip the weapon. What ever people previously bought in BF and BFs2, those items should be tagged as Legacy so they can still use it.

How will this benefit the game? Well say I bought tokens, and there's a sale going on. I want to be able to buy the item now to use for later, and still get the sale price. So for the game it self, the developers are still getting money.

How will this benefit players? They can obtain weapons at a cheaper price when its on sale.

In case people don't understand the "legacy" part, it's just so people who previously bought items before the level restrict, its now a level restrict equip not level restrict to buy. So instead of making 2 items, you make all the old ones Legacy ie. Legacy Moongun. So you can still equip one if you bought it before s3. But when you buy one s3 and so on, its just Moongun. There's no difference, but it just helps filter it out.

Also to help prevent people from accidentally buying it, either put a confirmation such as if im level 1 and I buy a level 10 weapon, have it say are you sure? or add a resell option for full money back only for items unequipable (for FORCE POINTS ONLY, not token users). more benefits for less p2w

title: Give People The Ability to Give Away Tokens and Points

posts.h:
Hey guys, Something I have noticed is some people in this game are loaded, however I have bought tokens before, and I know that sometimes you just have leftovers. I once had 67 left over, and I could not buy anything. Even if I used it to repair weapons, I think of it as a waste. I would rather give it away, and help someone else complete a purchase of some kind. There was one guy I once met who asked me to stand there while he kills me, so he can get enough points to register a map. Now, I had over 50k Points, so I would have helped him out without him having to shave down my K/D ratio, but there is no such option, so I can not. Why is teamwork encouraged in this game, but not the spirit of giving? If P2W players gave away these things, they would not seem that mean to the eye.

Another great implication would be the amount of User-based Tournaments, the prizes being points/tokens. This way, Even if someone buys tokens solely for a tournament they are hosting, the tokens ultimately go back into the system.

I however, understand that points are meant to be a prize for playing the game, If two friends killed each other constantly on a private room, and just transferred the points to one of them, it might be a bit discouraging, I admit. So in defense, I recommend a weekly send limit of 5K-10k Points That way, they would need to keep playing the game to get points beyond that amount. Tokens on the other hand are purchased and should act as that, purchased, and should be able to be sent as a gift. Where points on the other hand are like working to earn them.

Let me know what you think, I am sure there are implications I might not have gone over. I just want to help some people out.

Player A has potions
Player B has no potions

title: Being Able to Download Our Maps Offline

posts.h:
Hey guys, so I just had an idea:

How about Infernum makes the option to pay and download an Offline Brick-Force program that allows us to save our registered maps from the website to that program? Infernum could even sell this in CDs. It could let us save our maps that we worked so hard on to a USB our our computer hardware, with an option for offline multiplayer ( 2 or more people playing on one computer screen, but people can buy PC controllers), or at the very least let us fly around and admire our maps.

Many of us worked very hard on our maps, and I personally feel like we should have the option to have our maps with us at all time, because unfortunate things could happen such as people hacking our accounts. I'm sorry if there are some of you who get angry when Brick-Force gets compared to Minecraft, but there are many people who built miraculous things, and have no worries because their maps would be backed up on a USB or hard drive.

Again, the point of an offline Brick-Force program is to have (and maybe play) on our maps forever, no matter what happens to our account, or possibly the online version of Brick-Force itself.

Thank you for reading my idea.

posts.t: Fall deaths should be penalised, and assists should be acknowledged

posts.h:
Yes, it is obvious one can abuse self killing to heal themselves and/or gain back armour. This should have been changed a long, long, long, long, long, long, long, long, long, long... an insanely long time ago. The problem actually went all the way back to the closed beta. However, the issue was never up for too much debate because snipers killed in one hit regardless, so self killing didn't benefit a player unless he needed ammo or the enemy team didn't use snipers (which was unheard of back then). This doesn't just go for self killing by falling either. Explosive self kills are problematic as well. Often at times, people may choose the Rocket Launcher or other weapons that can kill themselves and their opponents at close range (like grenades). Some people may even purposely self kill themselves in mid combat with explosive weapons just to avoid their enemy getting a point. I've had it happen to me on more than one clan match.

The best method to solving self kills would be to give the kill to the enemy team "IF" the player was weakened by any of the enemy players. The player who last damaged the self killer or the one who got the most damage on him before his self kill would get the point, and score would actually be handed out properly to players then. Where as you can completely deprive newbies of any force points during a match if you were cheap enough to self kill against them before they could ever kill you. You could deprive them of a lot of force points if you used health potions and then committed suicide so they couldn't get any of that score for finally killing you. Which is a tactic I had seen a bit of in the EU server back in the day.

title: New Season 3 Weapons, Costumes, and More!

posts.h:
Well, if you read the title, you would know that I have come up with a boatload of things that can be added to Season 3. A lot of these are probably better on paper than in the game, but we'll see what people think. Most of these ideas are just things that I think that Season 3 is "lacking", or that I think would be cool regardless. I might add to my list of things later on, but for now, we'll just have to live with what I made so far. I'll put different categories into different posts, that way it'll be more organized.

And so, without further ado, I present to you my list of Season 3 ideas:

CLOTHES


I've come up with 4 costumes that I think would be cool for Brick-Force. For each clothing set, I'll list all the parts and their respective categories, as well as include my drawing of the outfit and in-game descriptions. Let's get to the first one, shall we?


Assassin Costume


Don't get me wrong, I like the Thief's outfit and all, but I thought that we might need something more... intimidating, I guess? Someone who looks like a master of stealth, rather than the burglar that the Thief's costume creates. And so, I made a few teaks to my old "Rogue Costume", and thus, the Assassin Costume was born.
Parts:
Assassin Hood [Headgear]
- The perfect hood for the perfect killer.
Assassin Shirt [Jacket]
- Become a master of stealth with this awesome looking outfit.
Assassin Pants [Pants]
- These boots are specially made to muffle footsteps. Your enemies better watch their backs!
Assassin Mask [Mask]
- You need this to hide your identity. It'd stink if someone knew who broke in.
Assassin Cape [Back]
- Know one really knows if assassin's wore capes or not. We just thought it fit the costume.
Assassin Medallion [Chest]
-Become a master of stealth with this awesome looking outfit.
Assassin Bag [Waist]
-Become a maser of stealth with this awesome looking outfit.


Ice Queen Costume


The initial thought that sparked this idea was that Brick-Force had a King and Princess outfit, but no Queen. Then, I decided that a normal queen would be boring, and so turned her clothes blue, and stuck "ice" into her name.
Parts:
Ice Queen Crown [Headgear]
- Sorry, this crown won't grant you magic powers, but it still looks nice regardless.
Ice Queen Cloak [Jacket]
- You can't be the queen, but at least you can dress like her.
Ice Queen Pants [Pants]
- You can't be the queen, but at least you can dress like her.
Ice Queen Necklace [Chest]
- Sorry, this necklace won't grant you magic powers, but it still looks nice regardless.
Female Brick-Head 2 [Character]
- You don't want brown hair? Have white hair instead!

Monk Costume


This is really more of a Martial Artist costume than a Monk costume. But since most people think of the 2 as related, I just called it the monk costume. I don't really have much more to say about this.
Parts:
Monk Headband [Headgear]
- Watch this headband increase your punching and kicking power to levels more than 9000!
Monk Robe [Jacket]
- Not only do you get this cool Martial Artist's uniform, but it also comes with your very own Black Belt!
Monk Pants [Pants]
- These pants were made specifically for making kicks more effective. We can't tell if it worked, though.


Overlord Costume


Originally, I was going to make a Viking costume, and then abandoned the idea for a "Dragon Knight". After thinking about a few more design ideas, I finally settled on "Overlord" and created this interesting suit of armor.
Parts:
Overlord Helmet [Headgear]
- This horned hat once belonged to Commander Brickgon, one of the most powerful Warlords in history.
Overlord Armor [Jacket]
- Wear this and become king of the battlefield! Includes snazzy shoulder-pads, too!"
Overlord Pants [Pants]
- Wear this and become king of the battlefield!
Overlord Cape [Back]
- This red cape only enhances your ability to intimidate others!
Overlord Scarf [Chest]
- Adding red to your wardrobe makes you seem even more intimidating than you already are!
posts.t: New Season 3 Weapons, Costumes, and More!

posts.h:
Weapons

I'll admit it right now: I'm a bit tired of seeing crossbows. Don't get me wrong, I love crossbows. But I just think that Infernum could afford to add a larger variety of weapons into the game. And so, here I am, with a list of new weapons we could have. None are crossbows. Not all are overly-effective weapons, but it adds a bit of variety, instead of just medieval crossbows. I'll include an image, in-game description, and weapon stats for each one.

Wyvern Cannon

- We're still not sure how ancient artificers managed to create a functioning wooden fire-blaster.

For a long time people have been requesting a flamethrower in Brick-Force. A long time, indeed. I ditched my "Dragon" weapon for the idea of a wooden fire blaster. Imagine something that shoots fireballs (Like the Dragon Staff) That slowly increase size over time, and doesn't explode. Now imagine something rapid-firing those fireballs. Seems pretty flamethrower-like to me. The major "con" to the Wyvern Cannon is that it can only work in short distances.
Main/Heavy
Stats:
Damage: 27%
Accuracy: 84%
Recoil: 30%
Rate of Fire: 67%
Ammo: 120
Mobility: 55%
Range: 20/40

Serpent Longbow

- Longbows were a popular ranged weapon before the crossbow was invented.

I really thought that a longbow would make a better long-range than a crossbow. After all, a longbow wouldn't really fit into any other category. So I took my favorite bow design from Final Fantasy XII, tweaked it a little, and created the first Brick-Force longbow. (It'd be cool if bow-string movements were implemented when it shoots ^^)
Main/Long
Stats:
Damage: 120%
Accuracy: 96%
Recoil: 60%
Rate of Fire: 7%
Ammo: 32
Mobility: 55%
Range: 100/140

Swarm Staff

- This staff was made with the finest wood and premium insect-attracting flowers to allow you to fight your battles with bugs!

What sparked my idea for this was something GraveBear said, something about him wanting there to be more "Magical" items in Brick-Force. Well, I guess this is for you, Grave. The Swarm Staff functions like any other light weapon, though it shoots bugs that sting your enemy when the come into contact. (Though the simple bullet animation would work, just change sound effects.)
Main/Light
Stats:
Damage: 23%
Accuracy: 98%
Recoil: 22%
Rate of Fire: 86%
Ammo: 150
Mobility: 65%
Range: 25/100

Whirlwind Staff

- Don't underestimate this bird just because it's small- it can blast your enemies with wind power!

This is another one of those "magical" weapons I mentioned earlier. This one blasting foes with wind rather than bugs, arrows, or bolts. This is another one of those weapons that will need some fancy animation too. My recommendation is that you re-color the Dragon Staff fireballs to make it white and light blue, resembling a wind blast. Every time the bird beats its wings, the wind blast is unleashed. Downside? You have to keep clicking for it to rapid-fire.
Main/Medium
Damage: 26%
Accuracy: 87%
Recoil: 29%
Rate of Fire: 67%
Ammo: 175
Mobility: 55%
Range: 65/140

Bat Sling

- It may be a cheap little slingshot, but just look at that ammo!

The bat sling was never meant to be one of the "best" secondary weapons. I just thought that it'd be cool to have this little toy in the BF aresenal. And, logically speaking, slingshots aren't any better than the weakest of pistols. Maybe the little band thing could move when it shoots, too? (But you gotta admit, that ammo capacity is out of control)
Secondary/Secondary
Stats:
Damage: 19%
Accuracy: 99%
Recoil: 32%
Rate of Fire: 37%
Ammo: 65
Mobility: 65%
Range: 35/100

Bricks

This section is pretty much just several bricks that I'd thought would be good for BF and fit the Season 3 theme. 2 Of them aren't even entirely original. After reading about one, just check the image above to see the block itself. They are organized in no particular way in the image.

General Bricks:

Castle Brick & Fortress Brick [Unlimited]
I notice a significant lacking of General Bricks in Season 3. The only thing added to that category was the newer wooden brick. That means if anyone wants to build large medieval buildings, they'd have to use the Season 1 bricks that they thought fit. And so I came up with the Castle and Fortress bricks, whose main purpose is for constructing massive medieval castles and towers. The 2 go hand-in-hand with each other, as they only real difference is the color; Castle Bricks are white with a slight tint of grey, while Fortress Bricks are dark and essentially coal-colored.

Function Bricks:

Trapdoor [Max. 10]
This is probably the Brick I want implemented most. Trapdoors, like the name applies, are 1 brick-sized doors that open automatically when someone walks on them. The reaction should be fast enough that if a person would run right over a trapdoor, they would still fall in unless they were standing on a separate brick as well. The trapdoor, when placed, appears on the top of the area it's in, unlike most flat bricks in Brick Force. Stepping on top of or coming into the area below a trap door automatically opens it, and it remains open for 2 seconds before closing again. (If a player is within the 'door's area when the 2 seconds are done, the timer resets again until the player leaves.) Once the doors open, the Trapdoor's area is pretty much treated like there's nothing there (That way, if 2 trapdoors were placed next to each other, players can't just run on the hinges of the 'doors to avoid falls), similarly to regular doors. (Man, this is complicated to describe.)

Yellow Portal [Max. 2]
I have not stressed this enough. I think that I lot of builders would enjoy it if there were 2 portals that anyone could use, rather than a single one. The Yellow Portal is identical to the Green Portal in every way other than colors.

Metal Door [Max. 15]
Here's one that's not entirely original. This is the Metal Door, as opposed to the Wooden Door. Metal doors are identical to the Wood ones function-wise, but there are a few differences. First off, it's metal, the appearance is different (But I bet you all have figured that out by now). Secondly, it's only 1x1x2 bricks large, making just the perfect size for a Brickman to squeeze through. This could make it more of a "side door", rather than the downright massive wooden door.

Vines [Unlimited]
This is really just another re-skin of a ladder. Vines work identically to ladders in every way, but they're more suited for nature-based maps, or, as suggested in another thread, could be some sort of "secret" when set up against the right type of brick.

I can assure you that the idea of this feature was not to remove skilled players from a room and this is more of "individuals abusing the feature" then anything. This feature was added as a way for players to remove those who absolutely need removed from a play room. Perhaps there is someone hacking in a lobby? As rare as this has become it in the past there was nothing that could be done to prevent them from ruining a match. This feature was requested by the community and is not something that noone has ever seen in a game, as I can think of several games that use a vote/kick system.

Now I am not saying that the system does not have its flaws as we have seen players are abusing this to remove players who give them a challenge instead of using it to remove players who cause problems or break the rules of the game itself. As your feedback is something that I collect on a weekly basis this was something that I made sure to include in my weekly report. I can only hope that the system is re-evaluated and a more fair system can be created using this function. A few flaws that are known with the vote/kick are the % needed to remove someone from a play room and that it can be used in clan matches. These are two things that I feel will be looked into and I for one think that this function should help to create a more enjoyable experience for others.

Thanks again for your feedback on this guys and I will include this again in my reports next week.
